00e972cdd95a1c4a: KUALA LUMPUR: Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan questioned why the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) did not clarify that his 12-year-old son was not required to attend its headquarters before he brought him there on Monday.
In a Facebook post today, Saravanan said they were only informed after entering the premises that his son was not required to sign anything and could return home.
"If he did not need to be there, why was this not clarified before a 12-year-old was brought to an anti-corruption headquarters?" he wrote.
Earlier, Saravanan criticised the agency's explanation, describing it as "entirely illogical" for his 12-year-old son to appear at its headquarters.
"With one child abroad, it was reasonable to understand that the other was my 12-year-old son," he said.
Saravanan said he had already informed MACC officers that his son was a minor and had no property in his name.
"Yet it was only after he walked through the doors of MACC headquarters that we were told he did not need to sign anything and could go home," he said.
He said MACC had since claimed that his son was never meant to be served and suggested that the family might have brought him because there was no one at home to look after him.
"This is ludicrous and never any parents' option to begin with," he said.
Saravanan also questioned MACC's position that the law imposed no age limit on such a notice.
He cited Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009, which provides for a person to furnish a statement on oath, with failure to comply carrying criminal consequences.
However, he said the legal system recognised that children might not have the capacity to understand the significance of an oath.
He cited Section 133A of the Evidence Act 1950, which provides for children of tender years to give unsworn evidence.
"So the question cannot simply be whether Section 36 contains the words '18' or '12'.
"It must also be whether applying an adult investigative mechanism to a 12-year-old produces an absurd and disproportionate result," he said.
Saravanan said Section 17A of the Interpretation Acts 1948 and 1967 required legislation to be interpreted in a manner consistent with its purpose and effect.
He said the issue was not merely whether the law technically allowed such a notice, but whether the process was appropriate when applied to a child.
On Sept 25, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman announced that asset declaration notices would be served on Saravanan, his wife and 3 children on Sept 28.
99c03dd40a1b4146: NAGOYA: Hosts Japan won their third straight Asian Games women's football gold on Friday, edging North Korea on penalties after a 2-2 draw in a dramatic final.
Yuzuho Shiokoshi scored the decisive penalty as Japan, who reached the final without conceding a goal, won 5-3 in the shootout to claim the title for the fourth time.
North Korea changed their goalkeeper in the final minute of extra time but it was not enough to give them their first gold since 2014.
The hosts looked in full control when Mami Ueno gave them the lead in the 32nd minute in Shizuoka.
But Jong Kum bundled in an equaliser two minutes into the second half that was eventually given after a VAR check, before Jon Ryong Jong put North Korea ahead in the 69th minute.
Japan's Hanon Nishio equalised with four minutes left to send the game into extra time.
The teams could not be separated and North Korea brought on substitute goalkeeper Chae Un Gyong to help their cause.
Instead it was Japan goalkeeper Shu Ohba who was the hero, stopping Jong's penalty in the only miss of the shootout.
North Korea were backed by groups of red-clad supporters among the crowd of over 6,000.
Japan and North Korea went into the final having each scored 26 goals in the previous rounds.
The two teams had also shared the previous six Asian Games titles, winning three each.
Japan coach Michihisa Kano won his first title since replacing Greenland-born Nils Nielsen.
Nielsen led Japan to the Asian Cup title in Australia in March but was fired 12 days later.
North Korea were looking to extend their astonishing recent run of international success in women's football.
They have won three world titles at age-group level in the last two years, and North Korean club Naegohyang Women's FC became Asian champions in May after a final tournament played in South Korea.

Women's football is one of the strongest international sports for diplomatically isolated and impoverished North Korea, with their national sides regularly competing at the highest levels in Asia and globally. --AFP

424dc82a56f2938f: PETALING JAYA: Former Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung has hit back at PKR deputy secretary-general Bryan Ng over criticism of his attendance at meetings involving the Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ).
Lee said in a statement this evening that an MP was not a member of MBPJ but was invited to council meetings as an observer, with no voting rights or authority to approve council papers.
However, the criticism from Ng, who is a city councillor, had focussed on how often Lee had attended MBPJ meetings rather than the policy issues he had raised, Lee said.

“My primary arena is the Dewan Rakyat, parliamentary committees and engagement with ministries. That is where the voice of Petaling Jaya is carried to the federal level,” he said. On the other hand, a city councillor is appointed to sit, scrutinise, debate and vote on matters before MBPJ.
Lee challenged Ng to disclose his own attendance record at council and committee meetings, as well as his position and voting record on the proposed Petaling Jaya Dispersal Link.
Lee also asked Ng to clarify whether MBPJ had approved or signed an agreement for the Selangor Intelligent Parking scheme and, if so, whether Ng had objected or recorded his dissent.
Lee also challenged Ng to state PKR’s official position on the two projects and on calls for a royal commission of inquiry into what he described as the “corporate mafia”.
Lee said his record on the issues was public, citing his opposition to the parking scheme, and his call for the PJD Link concession to be terminated.

“The people of Petaling Jaya, and PKR’s own members, deserve answers. If the party has a clear position, state it. If it does not, then the problem is not that I spoke up. The problem is that the party has stayed silent,” he said.
He added that attending meetings meant little if problematic projects were allowed to proceed without objection.

Ng had earlier criticised Lee for allegedly failing to attend most meetings on the Petaling Jaya local plan despite being invited as the MP. He said the plan was important in determining urban development, including land use, traffic, public facilities and the city’s future planning.
Earlier today, Lee, a one-term MP, announced that he was stepping down as the Petaling Jaya MP following his three-year suspension from PKR.

He said his suspension was likely due to his vocal stance on several issues, including the Urban Renewal Act, foreign worker recruitment, university admissions for STPM students, and Selangor’s guidelines on non-Islamic places of worship.
Lee, who plans to resign from the party on Monday, had been at odds with PKR’s leadership after attending the launch of Bersama in May.

f79917694a0f8e6f: OpenAI has fired two safety researchers and a program manager for allegedly mishandling sensitive company information. The ChatGPT maker confirmed the dismissals to The Register, saying an internal investigation found the trio had violated company rules governing access to and handling of confidential information. "We have parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information," an OpenAI spokesperson said. "Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work." At least some of the information was allegedly shared with an outside organization that evaluates AI systems. OpenAI said its investigation found other misconduct beyond that disclosure, but has not described it or identified the organization. The ChatGPT creator said the employees were not dismissed for raising AI safety concerns. The firings come after a messy few months for OpenAI's safety teams, including an incident in which one of its agents compromised infrastructure belonging to AI platform Hugging Face. OpenAI subsequently brought in external experts to investigate what happened and published findings detailing the agent's behavior and the security failures that allowed it to reach Hugging Face. The incident also prompted a much wider trawl through OpenAI's logs for other examples of agents interacting with external systems. This week, OpenAI said it has now notified more than 100 organizations about activity linked to its agents. Being contacted doesn't necessarily mean an organization was hacked or that private data was accessed. OpenAI said the notifications cover cases where agents interacted with third-party systems without authorization or in ways that warranted alerting their operators. OpenAI's investigation has also found cases where its agents sent training and evaluation data to third-party services. In 53 instances, images originally uploaded by ChatGPT users ended up on image-hosting sites. On September 20, an agent contacted an external chatbot through insufficiently filtered DNS traffic in a training environment intended to block live internet access. OpenAI's monitoring system spotted the behavior within 15 minutes and a human reviewer picked up the alert three minutes later, but the run wasn't actually killed for another two and a half hours. OpenAI has also scrapped the planned release of GPT-6.1 Astra after concluding the model didn't meet its safety bar around remaining within the scope and authorization of tasks it was given. The US biz hasn't said whether the allegedly mishandled material concerned any of its recent agent incidents, whether the outside organization was involved in investigating them, or whether any customer or user information was exposed. ®

21db9672de248c3c: EVOLELECTRIC Motors Sdn Bhd, the Malaysian distributor of JAC pickup trucks, has partnered with FT Assembly Sdn Bhd (FTA), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Feytech Holdings Bhd, to locally assemble JAC's T9 range in the country.
The phased completely knocked-down (CKD) programme will cover the T9 petrol plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV), diesel and battery electric vehicle (BEV) variants.
The T9 PHEV will lead the programme, followed by the diesel and BEV versions, with production scheduled to start in November 2026.
Initial annual capacity is estimated at 3,000 units.

FTA has invested RM3.6 million to establish the JAC assembly facility at Feytech's manufacturing plant in Kulim, Kedah, with total investment potentially reaching RM8 million over the next three years.
The 84,000 sq ft facility includes vehicle assembly, inspection, testing and quality-control operations.
The CKD programme targets local content of up to 30 per cent.
It is expected to generate about RM230 million in annual economic value and will create jobs while supporting the local automotive supply chain.
The locally assembled T9 PHEV and BEV are expected to be the first locally assembled PHEV and BEV pickup trucks in Malaysia.
This will extend the country's vehicle assembly capabilities into the light commercial new energy vehicle segment.
Evolvelectric Motors chief executive officer Lau Yit Mun said the programme would strengthen JAC's long-term presence in Malaysia.
"JAC Pickup together with Evolvelectric Motors is building a stronger foundation in Malaysia by producing its pickup trucks locally," he said.
JAC is also exploring potential exports of pickups from Malaysia, subject to market conditions.
The T9 PHEV, which will be introduced as a completely built-up model in early November, offers a combined range of up to 1,000km and up to 1,000Nm of torque from its dual-motor system.
It also carries a five-star ANCAP safety rating.
The locally assembled T9 PHEV is expected to roll out in November 2026, while the BEV is targeted for January 2027.

d8fb35fe53d34fad: WASHINGTON, Oct 2 — The unprecedented botched execution of a woman in Tennessee has reignited the debate over execution methods in the United States — which varies from lethal injection to firing squads.
Methods used in the US
Methods vary by state. States carry out the vast majority of executions, while federal executions are rare.
Lethal injection, authorised in 28 states and at the federal level, remains by far the most common execution method since the death penalty was reinstated in the United States in 1976.
Of the 47 executions carried out in 2025, 39 were by lethal injection.
Five others were by nitrogen inhalation, a method first used anywhere in the world in the southern state of Alabama in 2024 and likened by UN experts to a form of “torture.”
Three were by firing squad in South Carolina, marking the first use of that method in the United States since 2010.
But some states have struggled to obtain the necessary drugs from pharmaceutical companies reluctant to be associated with capital punishment.
This was the case, for example, in South Carolina, Utah and Indiana, which resumed executions in 2024 after suspending them for more than a decade for this reason.
In terms of frequency, electrocution and gas inhalation are, respectively, most common, each authorised in nine states, followed by firing squads, a method provided for in five states.
A litany of botched executions
No execution method is immune to the risk of spectacular failure.

In Alabama in 1983, John Evans’s leg caught fire after the first electric shock, while smoke rose from his hood and the smell of burning flesh began to fill the room. It took three shocks in all before the condemned man’s heart stopped beating.

In the northern state of Ohio in 2009, Romell Broom endured two hours of attempts by three members of the state’s execution team, who stuck needles into his arms, hands and legs 18 times in an effort to administer the lethal injection.
The first condemned prisoner to survive an execution attempt in the United States since 1946, he ultimately died of Covid-19 in his cell in December 2020.
Even firing squads, supposedly a more decisive method, present difficulties, Laura Porter, director of a coalition of US organisations campaigning to abolish the death penalty, told AFP.
During Mikal Mahdi’s execution in South Carolina in 2025, the shooters, “missed the target of the heart, and so it took longer for [him] to die,” she said, citing the autopsy findings.
Nitrogen inhalation was used “with severe, severe problems in Alabama,” and “it’s temporarily on hold,” she said.
“I don’t believe that there is a perfect way to kill people,” Porter said.
“Participating in execution is incredibly stressful and harmful to corrections officers,” she added.
Botched execution consequences
US states generally respond to the most shocking failures by imposing a moratorium to revise their execution protocols or by introducing new execution methods.
Tennessee imposed a moratorium in 2022 before resuming executions by lethal injection in 2025 under a revised protocol.
Alabama tried nitrogen inhalation in January 2024 following a botched lethal injection execution in November 2022.
But Porter said no lasting solution would be possible until the secrecy surrounding executions was lifted.

“When there are problems with protocols, or when there are problems with the drugs, or there are problems with the competency of the execution team, it is very, very difficult to obtain any information until after the problem has happened because we are given no information about the execution process,” she said. — AFP
58d8fc2f785d4a91: COPENHAGEN, Oct 2 — The international future of Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo hung in the balance after the 41-year-old walked out on the squad after learning that he would not start the game against Denmark yesterday.

Ronaldo announced late on Wednesday that he had left the team, shortly after a press conference in which coach Jorge Jesus confirmed the five-time Ballon d’Or winner would be left out of his starting line-up for a second consecutive Nations League game.
In his absence, Portugal turned on the style to beat Denmark 4-2.
The former Real Madrid forward had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium on the eve of the game, but walked out following the announcement by Jesus.

“Following the national team coach’s press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team’s training camp,” Ronaldo wrote on Instagram.
He had already spent the entirety of Sunday’s 2-1 Nations League win in Norway on the bench, having captained the side in the 1-0 home victory over Wales last Thursday.
Ronaldo appeared to indicate that the reasons behind Jesus’s decision ran deeper, and hinted at a departure from the national team he has graced for more than two decades.
“In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated,” Ronaldo said.
“Now is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception.”

Spanish sports daily Marca said that Jesus and Portuguese federation president Pedro Proenca followed Ronaldo to Copenhagen airport in an attempt to persuade him to stay with the squad, before the player boarded his private jet.

Jesus insisted earlier on Wednesday that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old, who was appointed in July, acknowledged that his captain was disappointed to remain on the bench against Norway.
The news sparked a wave of memes on social media and a furious backlash from Ronaldo’s sister, Elma Aveiro.
“They don’t deserve to have the best of anything,” she said about the Portuguese people on Instagram.
“We are envious, scornful, and ignorant, and we deserve to return to the mediocrity that defined us in the pre-CR7 era of football,” she added, using his nickname.
‘Players with status’
The game in Oslo was the first time since November 2024 that Ronaldo had not featured for Portugal while not being either injured or suspended.
“There was no incident whatsoever,” Jesus, who coached Ronaldo at Saudi club Al-Nassr for a year, insisted after that match.
“Any player — and I was a player myself... when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don’t get on... no one is happy about that,” Jesus added on Wednesday.
The Portuguese coach also said that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he might bring him on as a substitute.
“Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It’s nothing to make a fuss about,” Jesus insisted.
After the win yesterday, Jesus’ press conference was dominated by talk of Ronaldo.
“This Portugal team scored four goals and put in a performance which, in my opinion, was of a very high standard,” he said.
“Of course, this is more important than anything else that has happened.
“I still think exactly the same way: there are players with status. That much is crystal clear,” he added.
“But I’ll say it again: the rules are the same for everyone.”
There were reports that Portuguese Prime Minister Luis Montenegro had even discussed the issue of Ronaldo’s involvement with the coach on Wednesday.
Jesus said earlier in the day that against Denmark he again intended to start AC Milan striker Goncalo Ramos, who scored the winner in Norway.
Regarding Ronaldo, he said: “If I need him, he’ll come on. If I don’t need him, he won’t.”
Ronaldo recently announced that this would “probably (be) my last year in football”.
He is Portugal’s leading goalscorer and most capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.
The former Sporting, Manchester United, Real and Juventus striker made his international debut aged 18 in 2003 and played in the Euro 2004 final when Portugal lost to hosts Greece.
He reached the World Cup semi-finals in 2006 and captained his country to glory at Euro 2016.
Ronaldo and Portugal were eliminated by eventual winners Spain in the last 16 of this year’s World Cup. — AFP
9df1af8f937c1dba: PASIR MAS, Oct 2 — Rantau Panjang was once a bustling border town, alive with the pulse of trade; however, the passage of time and a decline in visitor numbers have left some premises quiet, while the remaining traders continue to hope for a turnaround.

The proposal to extend the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) alignment from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is seen not merely as a new transport option, but as a potential catalyst to revitalize economic activities in the town.

For those who have earned their livelihood there for decades, ECRL represents more than just tracks and trains; it offers a chance to see Rantau Panjang return to being a bustling, vibrant hub that draws crowds once again.

A Bernama survey of Rantau Panjang town found that while some businesses are operating as usual, others remain closed reflecting a shift in the business landscape compared to the vibrance locals once experienced.
For the traders who have persevered, customer volume is a key factor in business survival, consequently, any initiative to improve accessibility and the flow of people to the area is eagerly awaited.

Rantau Panjang resident Syed Abu Bakar Syed Daud, 65, who has lived in the area for over 50 years said he has personally witnessed the town's transformation, particularly regarding the number of visitors and traders.

Having started his business more than 44 years ago, he noted that the slump in commercial activity has impacted his own income, forcing him to close two grocery shops and an eatery over the past year.

“When this town was still ‘alive,’ over 1,000 traders operated here, but now fewer than 30 per cent remain, even though visitor numbers are merely modest. In the past, I could make over RM1,000 in daily sales, but before closing my shop, there were times when it was difficult to reach that amount even over two or three days,” he told Bernama recently.
According to Syed Abu Bakar, the shift became more pronounced following the Covid-19 pandemic, as visitor numbers and business activity in the town failed to return to previous levels.
He noted that the proposal to extend the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) to Rantau Panjang offers a glimmer of hope for traders who wish to see the area become a hub of activity once again.
“I was delighted to hear the news that the ECRL is set to be extended to Rantau Panjang. We certainly hope that more people will visit and that the town can come back to life,” he said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Trader Fu Chee Kat said changing customer patterns have forced him to scale back his business in Rantau Panjang, where he now operates just one shop with one employee. — Bernama pic
For trader Fu Chee Kat, 81, who has been doing business in Rantau Panjang for over 30 years, changing customer patterns have also impacted his operations.

He previously ran two shops selling various goods including kitchenware and bedsheets and employed six workers; however, he was forced to close one shop two years ago and now retains only one employee.
He added that one of the issues raised by customers is their concern regarding taxes on goods purchased in the area.

“There are customers who said they were reluctant to come and shop in this town due to concerns about being charged tax. There are times when they are taxed even after purchasing just a single item. Therefore, I hope the government will look into this matter and re-evaluate it, particularly regarding retail purchases; perhaps the tax could be abolished for retail and applied only to wholesale purchases,” he said.
Fu said if the ECRL extension materialises, the increase in visitor numbers could benefit local traders who still rely on commercial activities in the town.

In this regard, resident Rozila Salleh, 55, expressed deep appreciation of the Madani Government's under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over the focus on the development of Rantau Panjang.
She hopes the proposed ECRL extension would drive development and improve transport accessibility in the border area.
“Rantau Panjang is indeed one of the main gateways to Thailand, so extending the ECRL here would provide residents and visitors with another transport option alongside the current land routes.

“We greatly appreciate the Prime Minister and the Madani Government's attention to development in border areas like Rantau Panjang. We hope this initiative becomes a reality, as it would not only benefit residents but also open up broader economic opportunities for local traders,” she said.

Media reports previously indicated that Malaysia and China had agreed to the proposal to extend the ECRL project from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang, a move with the potential to establish a direct transport link with Thailand.

Anwar reportedly said the proposal could not only boost the economy of Kelantan’s interior which had previously seen limited development spillover but also strengthen cross-border transport connectivity.

In August, Transport Minister Anthony Loke reportedly said that ECRL Phase 1 (Kota Bharu to Gombak) is targeted to begin operations this December ahead of the original January 2027 schedule subject to the smooth progress of testing and commissioning processes, including System Integration Tests and the Fault-Free Run, without compromising safety. — Bernama
cd1b7ffee4a6e4fc: TOYOHASHI, Oct 2 — Taekwondo dates back more than 2,000 years, but on Friday at the Asian Games the Korean martial art stepped into a not-so-brave future where nobody gets hurt: virtual taekwondo.
At a gymnasium about a 90-minute drive from the main Games host city of Nagoya, a modest number of spectators watched with a mix of fascination and bewilderment.
Taekwondo officials have billed it as “real-world martial arts meets cutting-edge virtual technology”.
Competitors wear a VR headset and motion tracking technology allows their movements to control their in-game avatars.
They have “nodes” on their back, thighs and shins to pick up each bodily action.
Rounds are typically 60 seconds each and matches are a best of three rounds, the two combatants standing within their own play area a few metres apart.
The goal is to aim real-life kicks to the virtual body and head of their opponent to deplete their computerised health bar.
The opponent is physically there, standing on an opposing side, but there is never any real-life contact.
Darren Yap won bronze — to go with another bronze in the traditional format.
“It was fun playing out there. I had zero expectations,” said the Singaporean.
Asked what he could see through the VR headset, he said: “You can see your health bar, your opponent’s character, your limbs.
“It’s actually quite nice to wear.
“It’s a fun way to do sparring and it’s a fun way to do taekwondo without the contact.”
‘Groundbreaking’
Officials say virtual taekwondo is just as athletically demanding as the real thing, but safer.
Governing body World Taekwondo “proudly endorses” it, calling it “groundbreaking”.
Sceptics say it is just another type of gaming.
The first world championships were in 2024 in Singapore, but on Friday it arrived at a bigger stage.
One of the differences to the real-life sport is that men and women compete in a mixed category. There are also no weight classes.
“It allows more people to participate in the sport, and I think it’s cool that women are able to beat men,” said Yap, 22, after losing his semi-final to Vietnam’s woman athlete Chau Ngoc Tuyet Sang.
Singapore has become the early home of the sport. Virtual taekwondo appeared at the inaugural Olympic Esports Week in the city-state in 2023.
Silver medallist Chau, who also competes in the real-life format, had mixed feelings about no gender or weight separation.
“One advantage is that you don’t have to worry about the difference in weight,” the 21-year-old said.
“But one disadvantage is that men and women can have differences in physical strength, and men may tend to be stronger.
“That could also mean that some of the movements are faster than those performed by women.” — AFP
45509829b43de07e: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — December 11, 1993 marked one of the darkest moments in the nation’s disaster history when Block 1 of the Highland Towers Condominium in Ulu Klang, Selangor collapsed, claiming 48 lives.

The tragedy highlighted the need for a specialised search and rescue team capable of responding to large-scale disasters, leading to the establishment of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) on August 1, 1995.

More than three decades later, SMART has evolved into a Heavy Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) team that meets the standards of the International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) under the United Nations (UN).

SMART obtained Heavy USAR recognition through the INSARAG External Classification (IEC) in 2016 and recently successfully defended the recognition through the INSARAG External Reclassification (IER), with excellent results.
While the 2016 assessment involved about 130 checklists, the assessment on Sept 22 covered 173 elements across five main components: management, search, rescue, logistics and medical.

SMART Logistics Section head and INSARAG assessor Safrizan Suhaini, 45, said becoming an assessor required more than experience in a rescue team, as candidates must attend courses set by the UN, undergo the Classifier in Training process and have operational field experience.

Safrizan, who has been with SMART for 14 years, has participated in eight classification processes, including six as an assessor and two as a deputy head assessor, in countries including Japan, Oman, Hong Kong, New Zealand, France and Russia.
He said the experience provided opportunities for SMART to learn from international teams’ best practices and bring them back to be adapted to strengthen the national team.

“If we are not given the opportunity to go abroad and observe how others operate, we might feel we are the best. When we step out, we realise there are actually improvements that can be made within our team,” he told Bernama recently.

The knowledge-sharing process is now two-way, with seven of SMART’s practices identified as best practices by 11 international assessors during the latest assessment, including in medical care, logistics management and operations.
Safrizan said these practices would be brought to the UN level and shared through the USAR network for adaptation by teams in other countries.
“They do not only look at our shortcomings, but they also take away the positive aspects. This enhances our capacity and capability so that we are always improving,” he said.

Meanwhile, SMART training officer PgKB II Mohamad Hafiezul Abdul Halim said defending the status through the IER was more challenging as the assessment was based not only on exercises but also on the team’s track record over the previous two years, including operations, training, equipment and medical aspects.
He said the INSARAG methodology was also reassessed every five years based on current developments and needs, requiring the team to continuously enhance its capabilities.

Mohamad Hafiezul, who has served as an INSARAG assessor in China and France, said discipline and multitasking skills were among SMART’s strengths, with members trained to assist other components when required.
He added that technology, such as high-capacity drones equipped with thermal imaging, was also becoming increasingly important in accelerating the search for victims.
“If we cannot find the victims, how can we rescue them? Once we can determine the victims’ locations, we can then proceed to rescue them,” he said.
For a team born out of the Highland Towers tragedy, SMART’s success today goes beyond defending its international status, reflecting the evolution of Malaysia’s SAR capabilities.

More than three decades later, Malaysia is no longer merely learning from how the world conducts SAR operations. Through SMART, the country’s experiences and practices now have the potential to be shared with the global rescue community. — Bernama
0d5bf5d44b292259: Although I count the original Game Boy as one of my first tech obsessions, I still consider Nintendo’s Game Boy Advance to be my favorite console of all time thanks to its more comfortable horizontal design (for my big hands) and its expansive catalog of excellent 32-bit and 16-bit games. Ayaneo isn’t the first company to attempt to modernize the GBA, but its Konkr Pocket Advance does it best. The handheld strikes a near perfect balance between authentically re-creating the GBA’s design while updating its hardware with new controls, a much better screen, and the flexibility of Android at a price that feels like a bargain.

As much as I still adore the GBA, I’ve eagerly embraced upgrades to the aging console over the years. First it was the clamshell GBA SP that finally delivered a frontlit screen I could actually see without a lamp over my shoulder, and later it was aftermarket upgrades like a backlit LCD display and a rechargeable battery that vastly improved Nintendo’s original hardware. Two years ago, I eagerly purchased Anbernic’s GBA-inspired RG34XX, but all of those have now been replaced by the Konkr Pocket Advance.

It’s my first handheld from Ayaneo, and I’ve been pleasantly surprised to find the hardware feels on par with Nintendo’s. The Pocket Advance is an all-plastic affair but with a satisfying heft thanks to extra internal hardware including a cooling fan for its MediaTek Helio G90T processor and a 4,000mAh battery. I opted for the cheaper $109 version with 3GB of RAM and 32GB of storage, which is expandable with a microSD card, but for $129, you can get 4GB of RAM with 64GB of storage built-in.

It’s not an exact copy of the GBA, but the Pocket Advance’s dimensions are close enough to fit all the cases I’ve somehow preserved for the past 25 years. Where Ayaneo’s remake really diverges from the original is with eight additional buttons including X and Y action buttons plus four extra shoulder buttons on the top edge. I’m a big fan of the larger D-pad Ayaneo has included, but some retro gaming purists may not be fans of how soft and squishy the Pocket Advance’s buttons all feel. I’ve had to learn to mash the action buttons just a little harder to ensure presses are always registered, but I don’t necessarily think the button feel is a downside because they’re also satisfyingly quiet.

The Pocket Advance’s 3.5-inch LCD touchscreen with a glass cover is an excellent upgrade, but it does cater to GBA games with a 3:2 aspect ratio and a 960×640 resolution allowing them to be perfectly scaled at 4x. (The GBA had a 240×160 screen resolution.) Unless you’re a monster who can tolerate playing games that have been stretched vertically or horizontally to fill a screen, emulating games from other systems will result in letterboxing or pillarboxing on the sides, and potentially some visual artifacts from scaling when the math isn’t perfect.

Most similarly sized and similarly priced handhelds run some variation of Linux. There’s a thriving community of developers creating and porting a large assortment of emulators, games, and apps to Linux, but installing, configuring, customizing and updating software is not always a user-friendly process, especially for novices who may only be familiar with using plug-and-play game carts. The Pocket Advance instead comes with Android 12, and while that version feels a little dated, setting up the handheld will feel a little more familiar to anyone with smartphone experience.
An authentic but upgraded clone of Nintendo’s Game Boy Advance that can play more than just GBA games using emulation.

Getting the Pocket Advance up and running was relatively easy thanks in part to Ayaneo’s custom launcher called AYASpace that makes it easier to install various emulators. But the handheld also has access to the Google Play Store, or you can install Android apps or add-ons downloaded directly from a website.

I’m a big fan of a clean and simple launcher for Linux handhelds called MinUI, so instead of AYASpace, I installed an alternative Android launcher called Cannoli on the Pocket Advance that brings the same aesthetics with several emulators preinstalled and preconfigured. The flexibility of Android means I can set the Pocket Advance to load Cannoli by default, but I have the option to switch back to AYASpace at any time, or install and jump between multiple alternatives.

When it comes to emulation capabilities, you’ll want to keep your expectations limited to “retro” gaming. The Pocket Advance’s seven-year-old processor is powerful enough to handle many titles from the PS2 and GameCube, but the handheld is better equipped to emulate the PS1 and Sega Dreamcast, and you’ll have the best experience with games from even older consoles like the Super Nintendo and Genesis. An easy-access quick settings menu that slides in from the right lets you quickly customize and reconfigure the handheld including boosting its performance (at the cost of battery life) to handle more intensive games, but another thing preventing the Pocket Advance from playing more modern games is its lack of analog thumbsticks.

Performance and compatibility will also vary with native Android games and apps. I’ve had a lot of fun playing through Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder’s Revenge once again, but while the Pocket Advance is a passable way to stream Netflix, I can’t get it to play any Disney Plus content without the app crashing out.

Anbernic’s $69.99 RG34XX is still cheaper than the Pocket Advance and may seem like a better alternative, but I think Ayaneo’s is absolutely worth the extra $40. It’s a more powerful and capable handheld with a higher-res display, and I much prefer the Pocket Advance’s larger D-pad and shoulder button arrangement. I also find the quality of Anbernic’s hardware to be hit and miss. Similar to what others have reported on Reddit, I’ve experienced intermittent issues with the responsiveness of the RG34XX’s D-pad. I haven’t had the motivation to crack it open to attempt a DIY fix, and with the Pocket Advance now in my collection, it’s doubtful I ever will.

The Pocket Advance is one of the best retro handhelds currently available and not just because of its nostalgic retro design. As long as you temper your gaming expectations and won’t be frustrated by what it can’t play, it’s an excellent way to revisit and enjoy games from Nintendo’s earlier handheld era.

98ff827a9febc8d1: In an effort to provide a more affordable AI system, Nvidia is introducing a cut down version of the DGX Spark with half the memory and storage. The GB10-based systems will be offered exclusively through hardware partners including Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, and MSI, and are expected to retail for around $4,999. The less-powerful SKUs are necessary after Nvidia jacked the price of its 128 GB DGX Spark on Friday to $6,950 — an increase of nearly 75 percent from this time last year. As you might have already guessed, skyrocketing memory prices are to blame for the massive price adjustment. That makes the 64 GB model considerably less than Nvidia’s top-spec DGX Spark and GB10 systems given the ongoing memory shortage, but that’s still 25 percent more than the 128 GB version retailed for at launch. Nvidia’s GB10 platform has been plagued by pricing creep since the Projects Digits concept was unveiled at CES last year. Originally, the appliance was expected to retail for around $3,000, not the $4,000 it eventually ended up selling for. Even at that price, the DGX Spark offered something that just a few years ago would have set you back tens of thousands of dollars: large quantities of GPU memory. In fact, at the time it launched, the system was technically the highest capacity workstation GPU Nvidia sold. That’s not really the case with the 64 GB model, which due to its smaller capacity, isn’t as well suited to certain AI workloads like fine tuning. But if your main concern is local AI inference for powering private agents, Nvidia argues models in the 26-35 billion parameter range, Qwen 3.8 27B for example, are now good enough to get the job done. While the new systems may offer less memory, we’re told the memory bandwidth remains unchanged at 273 GB/s, which tells us they’re using lower capacity LPDDR5x memory modules rather than fewer of them. Nvidia also says that beyond the new memory config, the systems are otherwise unchanged and will feature the same 20-core Arm processor from MediaTek. The systems also retain their onboard ConnectX-7 networking, which enables clustering of up to 4x GB10-based devices at 200 Gbps a piece. To further facilitate this, Nvidia says later this month it’ll be rolling out new software tools to DGX OS to facilitate cluster configurations and inference deployments. Previously, this required some tinkering in the CLI to get set up along with some tweaks to the vLLM or TensorRT-LLM launch commands. While the 64 GB version’s lower MSRP should make the systems more accessible amid the ongoing memory crunch, it doesn’t bode well for Nvidia’s RTX Spark notebooks and mini PCs expected to make their debut this fall. These systems are based on the same GB10 silicon that powers the DGX Spark and other DGX OS-based systems, but are intended for more general purpose computing, like AAA gaming, web browsing, and content creation, not just AI inference and training workloads. Announced at Computex late this spring, RTX Spark-based systems were already expected to be quite expensive, particularly the 128 GB variants. With DGX Spark pricing nearing $7,000, similarly equipped RTX Spark notebook offerings based on the chip could end up selling for significantly more. But, as we understand it, Nvidia will be offering versions of the chip with much lower memory capacities for price conscious PC buyers. However, across the DGX and RTX Spark lines, Nvidia will face some competition from AMD’s newly launched Gorgon Halo SoCs, which offer memory capacities ranging from around 32 GB at the low end to 192 GB for the top-spec Ryzen AI Max+ 495 SKUs. What’s more, systems powered by that chip are currently retailing for less than Nvidia’s 128 GB DGX Spark. But while AMD wins on max capacity, it should be noted that our testing has repeatedly shown that the GB10’s GPU offers substantially higher performance for AI tasks. ®

ef083c0ca8ea1525: DUNGUN: A 25-year-old medical assistant drowned while swimming at Chemerong Waterfall here today.

Al-Muktafi Billah Shah Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Kama Suhaimi Abdullah said the victim, Mohd Ikmal Awid, who was stationed at Kemaman Hospital, was found at the scene at noon.
He said the department received a report on the incident at 11.46am, but firefighters who arrived at the scene found that the victim, from Kota Belud, Sabah, had already been located by his friends.
"The victim was said to be swimming with six of his friends when suddenly he and another friend were swept away by strong currents," he said in a statement.
Suhaimi said the victim's friend was rescued by their friends, but the victim could not be saved.

5997ca5c692dcb62: KUANTAN: Two men were arrested after 56 compressed bricks of ganja weighing 58.1kg and worth RM174,000 were seized in Maran on Monday.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the suspects, aged 44 and 30, were detained around 1.20am while allegedly transferring four bags from the boot of a car in front of a homestay.
He said checks on the bags found 56 transparent plastic wrappers and aluminium foil containing dried compressed lumps suspected to be ganja.
"The current market value of the seized ganja is estimated at RM174,000 based on the price of RM3,000 per kilogramme," he told a press conference at the Pahang police headquarters here.
Azry Akmar said investigations found that the syndicate's modus operandi was to deliver drug supplies to areas where there was demand.
He said both suspects, believed to be from a northern state, admitted receiving RM10,000 to deliver the drugs to Maran.
"It is understood that this is the first time the group from the north carried out a delivery to the East Coast, specifically Pahang, as they previously operated mostly in the Klang Valley," he said.
He said background checks found that both men had previous drug-related records.
He added that the suspects had been remanded for seven days, from Monday to Sunday, to facilitate investigations under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act.
The case is also being investigated under Section 15(1)(a) of the same Act after preliminary urine tests on both suspects returned positive for methamphetamine, he said.
Meanwhile, Azry Akmar said Ops Hawk, conducted statewide across Pahang over three days from Monday, led to the arrest of 365 individuals.
He said the arrests comprised 79 for drug supply offences, 90 for drug possession, 191 for urine-related offences and five under special preventive measures.
Drug seizures worth RM221,190 were also recorded during the operation.
75220ee7fd4cfca3: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM) has called for a formal system to be set up to ensure that investigations are carried out and action taken on wastage and leakages flagged in the auditor-general's reports.

PSM chairman Dr Michael Jeyakumar Devaraj said a standard procedure should be set up after the auditor-general comes out with a report, "which gives many examples of leakages, including items being bought at three to five times the price".
“All this comes out in the news, but after that, it goes quiet,” he said at a press conference on PSM’s proposals for the 2027 budget.
Jeyakumar called for the auditor-general’s office to be strengthened, including by increasing its manpower to scrutinise wastage in government spending.

In its proposals, PSM questioned whether government agencies were required to investigate possible abuses of power highlighted in auditor-general reports, and whether the outcomes of such investigations were reported to higher authorities and made public.
It said the auditor-general’s work should result in concrete changes and greater professionalism among government agencies.
The 2026 Auditor-General’s Report Series 1, tabled in February, identified 273 issues involving financial management and governance at the federal and state levels.
Among them were irregularities involving Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, where an unauthorised cooperative collected RM50.74 million in student fees.

Other proposals raised by PSM include reducing the My50 public transport pass from RM50 to RM30, increasing funding for low-cost strata apartment maintenance to RM200 million, and easing tertiary education costs for low-income groups.

PSM also proposed establishing a child poverty database and providing greater nutritional support for children, imposing tighter conditions and taxes on data centres, and allocating RM1 billion for a joint initiative with Indonesia to tackle transboundary haze.
798c483e45b9a3cf: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Maritime industry expert Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan today questioned why an international maritime trade issue involving petroleum cargo worth more than RM220 million had yet to receive a clear answer from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), when the commission had moved swiftly on cases involving politicians.

Jeyenderan, who is chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, directed his questions at the MACC chief commissioner over a report he lodged on June 5. It concerns alleged discrepancies between the bill of lading and the physical movement of petroleum cargo at Tanjung Langsat, Johor.

“Why is the MACC continuing to remain silent on this issue? Why does it appear that cases involving politicians are being given special attention, while an issue involving international maritime trade has yet to receive a clear answer?” he said in a statement today.

He said that despite several visits to the MACC office and submitting various documents to the authorities, he had yet to receive a final written explanation on the status of the report or any decision made on it.

“I received four emails beginning in June and an SMS in September stating that the case was under ‘MACC Action’, but it has now been four months and there is still no final decision on the report,” he said.

“I have seen several politicians and corporate figures charged in court since May, including former ministers, former senior government officials and company executives, while my report has yet to receive a clear written decision.

“Just tell us whether the case is NFA (No Further Action) or still under investigation. If it is still being investigated, tell us. If it is NFA, tell us. Do not continue to remain silent. We only want to know the status of the report,” he said.

Jeyenderan said he had provided the documents and information requested by the authorities and was not seeking special treatment, only confirmation of whether the matter was still under investigation or had been concluded.

He said the matter should not be viewed as merely a local commercial issue, as it involved international petroleum cargo, trade documentation, Customs procedures, cargo traceability and government revenue.

Jeyenderan also claimed that the Royal Malaysian Customs Department had yet to provide a final written position on the Customs treatment of the cargo, despite repeated requests and discussions with the relevant authorities.

“The MACC is silent and Customs is also silent. We are talking about an international petroleum trade issue involving cargo worth more than RM220 million, yet there is still no proper written explanation on the regulatory position concerning the matter,” said Jeyenderan who has three decades of experience in the industry.

He claimed the absence of a written position had left industry players uncertain on several matters, including the handling of petroleum cargo declared under the K8 procedure, its discharge and storage in shore tanks, and whether mixing or blending it with existing stock was permitted and subject to specific approvals or documentation.
“How can businesses, traders and international players have confidence in the system if the authorities do not provide a clear position on the applicable procedures and requirements?

“We had a meeting with the Ministry of Finance last week. They concluded that no duty was imposed on the cargo as presented. But to date, no authority has provided any explanation in writing,” he said.
Jeyenderan alleged that the prolonged uncertainty could affect not only the parties directly involved but also Malaysia’s reputation as a trade and maritime hub.

He said he respected the investigative and regulatory powers of the MACC and the Customs Department, and understood that certain information might not be disclosed while an investigation was ongoing, but stressed that a clear written position should be provided when legally permissible.

He added that he would continue seeking clarification through the appropriate channels, saying his aim was to obtain certainty on the applicable procedures and documentation requirements, not to secure any particular decision in favour of his company.
e9f9e4db8f23296a: BEIJING: Aryna Sabalenka sent down 11 aces as she dismissed Renata Zarazua 6-1, 6-3 to launch her China Open title charge on Friday in Beijing.

fd65e2ba0f5c92bf: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) for 2026 is projected at 5.4 per cent, underpinned by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electric and electronic (E&E) exports, according to RHB Group.

In RHB's Global Economics Outlook for Q4 2026, group chief economist and head of market research, Barnabas Gan said the bank revised the headline inflation forecast to 1.9 per cent for 2026 from 2.1 per cent previously, reflecting softer-than-expected price pressures.
For the first eight months of the year, inflation averaged 1.8 per cent, alongside the restoration of the BUDI95 monthly quota and an increase in the diesel subsidy quota from September.
"For the rest of 2026, the inflation trajectory will be shaped by global commodity price movements, changes in domestic policies, as well as potential upside from food inflation," he said.

Gan added that domestic policy measures, such as RON95 and diesel subsidy, stable food prices, stable demand conditions and a relatively stable ringgit, as well as gradual pass-through to consumer prices should help keep inflation contained.
Meanwhile, he said the overnight policy rate is expected to remain unchanged at 2.75 per cent at the upcoming November Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting amid manageable inflation.

Moving forward, Gan said RHB Bank expects Bank Negara Malaysia to deliver a token 25 basis points (bps) hike in the first half of 2027 (1H 2027) as a normalisation move towards a more neutral policy setting rather than a response to significant inflationary pressures.

He also expects the 2026 fiscal deficit to remain broadly on track towards the government's 3.5 per cent of GDP target, although risks are tilted towards a modest overshoot given the relatively high deficit in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026) and uncertainties surrounding fuel subsidy expenditure.
At the same time, the bank is maintaining its current account surplus forecast at 2.4 per cent of GDP for 2026, versus a 2.5 per cent surplus in 1H 2026.

"The goods surplus should remain supported by resilient E&E exports amid the global technology cycle, while robust tourism receipts and information and communication technology services exports should underpin the services account.
"Together, these should sustain Malaysia's current account surplus," added Gan.
60bc259bc4f19de6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — High-performance transformation coach Syed Mohammad Murad Syed Naseem, better known as Coach Murad or Murad Zaidi, wants to know who was behind an Instagram account that allegedly posted death threats against social media influencer Caprice and his family, after police decided to take no further action against him.

His lawyer, Aizzat Mustafa, said Murad had initially been investigated in connection with the account, “jefri_yayan”, but was later informed by police that further action against him had been classified as No Further Action (NFA).
However, police confirmed in a written response dated Sept 18 this year that the underlying case remained open and under investigation, he said.

“On July 11 last year, Murad Zaidi was arrested in connection with the investigation. His mobile phone was seized, his residence was searched and several individuals connected to him were also called in to assist in the investigation.
“On Nov 26 last year, police informed Murad Zaidi in writing that the matter against him had been classified as NFA, following which his mobile phone was returned.
“My client has consistently denied being behind the account and cooperated fully with the police investigation,” Aizzat said.
The matter dates back to July 7 last year, when the account allegedly posted comments containing threats, including references to death and bullets, concerning Caprice and members of his family.

Aizzat said the latest position raised two important questions: who was actually behind the account, and why the matter remained unresolved more than a year after the alleged threats were first reported.

“The alleged threats were treated with considerable seriousness and urgency from the outset. Within days, Coach Murad was arrested, his telephone was seized, his residence was searched and persons connected to him were called in for investigation.
“More than a year has now passed. PDRM has confirmed that further action against Coach Murad was classified as NFA, yet the underlying case remains under investigation.

“In those circumstances, my client is entitled to ask what progress has been made in identifying the actual person behind the account and why the investigation has taken this length of time to reach a conclusion,” he said.
Aizzat stressed that Murad was not alleging that police had abandoned the investigation.

“PDRM has expressly confirmed that the matter remains under investigation. What Coach Murad is seeking is clarity on the progress of that investigation and, ultimately, the identity of the person responsible for the account and the alleged threats,” he said.
He said there was also a legitimate question over Caprice’s current position.

“We would like Caprice’s current position to be established, including whether he still maintains that Coach Murad was behind the account and whether he has received any subsequent information from PDRM concerning the identity of the actual operator.

“The allegations had serious consequences for my client and affected his reputation. Now that further action against him has been classified as NFA, he wants the public record to accurately reflect that position,” he said.
Aizzat said Murad had denied being behind the account from the outset and had himself lodged police reports over the matter.
“My client is not seeking confidential information which may prejudice an ongoing investigation.

“He simply wants an investigation which began with considerable urgency more than a year ago to reach a proper conclusion, and for the actual person responsible for the alleged threats to be identified.
“If Coach Murad was not the person against whom further action was ultimately taken, the obvious question remains: who was actually behind ‘jefri_yayan’?” he said.
Aizzat added that Murad hoped the investigation would be concluded without further delay so the matter could finally be clarified for all parties concerned.
526a372784eced57: SHAH ALAM: Sultan Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah bertitah kepada pemimpin politik supaya tidak bergaduh, bertelagah atau berebut kuasa sehingga mencetuskan perpecahan sesama sendiri.

bc84f760c4cf882b: SEPANG: Mercedes driver George Russell and Red Bull's Max Verstappen found the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) a demanding challenge during today's opening two free practice sessions, with soaring temperatures and heavy tyre degradation making it difficult to find the right set-up for this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
Formula 1 returned to the iconic circuit for the first time in nine years, since the 2017 Malaysian Grand Prix, with the heat and ageing tarmac taking a toll on both drivers and tyres.

Russell, making his first appearance at Sepang, admitted Mercedes had yet to find the right balance, while Verstappen said Red Bull still had plenty to work on despite topping the opening practice session.
Verstappen clocked the fastest lap of the day in FP1 with 1:37.520, while Ferrari's Charles Leclerc edged him in FP2 with a time of 1:37.528 as the punishing heat tested the drivers.
Rain later offered some relief from the sweltering conditions.
Russell posted 1:37.903 in FP1 to finish behind Verstappen but struggled in the second session, clocking 1:38.020 to end up seventh.
"It was a really cool experience driving this circuit. I've never driven here before. It's a really iconic place, so that was cool," said Russell.

"But with these conditions, tyre degradation is huge for everybody. The cars are operating in a very different window. We just haven't got the car quite where we need it to be. We need to make some set-up adjustments because we're a bit off the pace.
"I think I'm feeling the downforce in some of the corners, but with this amount of tyre overheating and tyre degradation, that kind of trumps everything.
"We just need to get on top of that overnight. That's more of a set-up issue rather than the upgrade itself, and we'll go from there."
Verstappen, who won the 2017 Malaysian Grand Prix, also acknowledged the challenges posed by the scorching track, saying Red Bull still had plenty to figure out.

"I think we had a decent start, but it's tricky. The track is really hot, with a lot of degradation, so there are a lot of things to figure out. But it's been positive," said the four-time world champion.

The Dutchman opted to stay on medium tyres during the latter stages of FP2 rather than chase a quicker lap on the soft compound, focusing instead on gathering long-run data as rain threatened the session.
"I wanted to do a long run in case there was some rain coming in," Verstappen said.

"Progress is difficult. It's always warmer again in FP2, with different programmes, so it's hard to say whether we've made progress. But there's still a lot of things to look at and try to understand better."

Russell was impressed by Verstappen's pace and that of McLaren's Lando Norris, who finished third in FP2 with 1:37.665, but insisted Mercedes would not give up the fight for victory after just two practice sessions.
"Currently, I think Verstappen looks very fast, and the race pace in McLaren looked very quick. But you know, never say never," he said.

Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton, now racing for Ferrari and the winner of the 2014 Malaysian Grand Prix, also showed encouraging pace, clocking 1:37.833 in FP2.The third free practice session and qualifying will be held tomorrow.
8a84533241c3aa43: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is likely to focus on improving tax collection and fine-tuning existing taxes rather than introducing major new levies in 2027 Budget, according to KPMG senior tax policy adviser Dr Veerinderjeet Singh.
He said stronger enforcement, better use of tax agency analytics and broader tax bases could provide additional revenue while supporting the government's fiscal consolidation efforts.
Speaking at a forum hosted by CIMB Securities, Veerinderjeet said the government should "sweat our assets".

This is by improving collection efficiency, with scope to gradually raise Malaysia's tax-to-gross domestic product ratio towards 15 per cent through stronger personal, corporate and indirect tax bases.
He expects few major tax changes in the upcoming budget, given the continued focus on cost-of-living support and social spending.

Recent measures such as the dividend and capital gains taxes reflect a more progressive tax system, although he does not expect the two per cent dividend tax to be raised or capital gains tax extended to listed shares in the budget.
A further increase in the 30 per cent top personal income tax rate also appears unlikely.

On the sales and service tax (SST), Veerinderjeet estimates coverage has reached about 78-80 per cent of goods and services, bringing it closer to the breadth of the former goods and services tax (GST).
He sees scope for broader input exemptions under SST to reduce cascading effects and business costs, although this would mean some revenue loss.
GST reinstatement is not expected in thr 2027 Budget, with improving SST efficiency likely to take precedence.
Wider e-invoicing participation could also help uncover unreported taxable activity, although exemptions for smaller businesses may be gradually reduced as economic conditions improve.
On other measures, Veerinderjeet expects limited additional revenue from the global minimum tax until the first filing cycle provides clearer evidence of collections.
A carbon tax remains on the policy agenda but could be delayed to 2028 or later amid business cost pressures.
The budget may reaffirm the government's intention to introduce it, potentially at a low initial rate.
He also sees only a slight possibility of modest excise duty increases on alcohol and tobacco, while no new windfall levy is expected.

For real estate investment trusts, he does not expect the former 10 per cent final withholding tax on distributions to return, although he supports withholding mechanisms to reduce filing and monitoring costs.
c1aa5a366969e734: JERUSALEM: Israel's elections commission has fined national security minister Itamar Ben Gvir for a video he posted on X in which he threatened to "put to death" a Palestinian prisoner, arguing the footage was electoral propaganda.

Far-right minister Ben Gvir, who is hoping to become defence minister under the next government, frequently appears in videos confronting inmates in Israeli prisons. The latest footage features convicted Hamas official Hassan Salameh.

Israel's Central Elections Committee ruled on Thursday that Ben Gvir must delete the video and pay 10,000 shekels (around US$3,250) each to two rights groups that had filed a petition against the footage.

According to the decision seen by AFP, the commission fined Ben Gvir not because of the content of the video but because it deemed he had violated election rules by campaigning for the Oct 27 vote by publishing the footage.
"The video is considered electoral propaganda," and it has been "established that public funds were used" to make it, the decision said.
The Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI), one of the two rights groups that had lodged a complaint, welcomed the decision on Friday.

"We hope that the repeated rulings of the elections committee will deter the minister from further using prisons as though they were his private property and humiliating prisoners as part of his election propaganda," PCATI legal director Merav Ben-Zeev said in a statement.
Ben Gvir published the video last month on X and has since deleted the post, but the footage is still available elsewhere online.
In the footage, the minister is seen in a prison cell confronting Salameh, a Palestinian prisoner sentenced to multiple life sentences for deadly attacks in Israel in 1996.
The video shows Salameh, frail and sporting a long beard, standing silently while Ben Gvir says, "I want to kill you. I want to put you to death."

In the caption, Ben Gvir wrote, "As national security minister, I led a policy that turned his life into hell. And with God's help, as defence minister, I will act to have murderous terrorists like him executed."
Ben Gvir is well-known for his inflammatory remarks and for posting videos of inmates.
He published one in August 2025 that showed him confronting the most high-profile Palestinian detainee in Israeli custody, Marwan Barghouti, in his prison cell.
In October of that year, he posted a video of himself standing over a row of Palestinian prisoners lying prone with their hands tied, in which he called for the "death penalty for terrorists".
Israel has since passed a death penalty law tailored to apply to Palestinians only, whose adoption Ben Gvir celebrated with a champagne toast.
3fbffcf1cba4c6b3: PETALING JAYA: Timbalan Presiden MIC M Saravanan petang tadi memperhebat kritikannya terhadap Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) berhubung keputusan memanggil anak lelakinya yang berusia 12 tahun ke ibu pejabat agensi itu untuk diserahkan notis pengisytiharan harta.

Bekas menteri sumber manusi itu berkata, anaknya itu menemaninya ke ibu pejabat agensi antirasuah berkenaan kerana beliau difahamkan bahawa kanak-kanak 12 tahun itu perlu hadir sendiri bagi menerima notis, susulan kenyataan Ketua Pesuruhjaya SPRM Abd Halim Aman pada 25 Sept.

Bulan lepas, Abd Halim dilaporkan berkata, notis itu akan diserahkan kepada Saravanan, isterinya dan dua anak mereka, manakala seorang lagi anak perempuan yang berada di luar negara akan menerimanya pada November.
“Dengan seorang anak berada di luar negara, wajar difahami bahawa seorang lagi itu merujuk kepada anak lelaki saya yang berusia 12 tahun,” kata Saravanan menerusi hantaran di Facebook hari ini.

Bagaimanapun, Abd Halim dilaporkan berkata semalam, SPRM menggunakan budi bicaranya dan 'mempertimbangkan apa yang munasabah' dalam memutuskan untuk tidak menyerahkan notis pengisytiharan harta kepada anak lelaki Saravanan.
Beliau berkata, kehadiran kanak-kanak berusia 12 tahun itu di ibu pejabat SPRM tidak bermakna dia berada di situ untuk menerima notis berkaitan siasatan berkenaan.
Anak-anak Saravanan kemungkinan besar hadir kerana tiada sesiapa di rumah untuk menjaga mereka, tambahnya.

Hari ini, Saravanan mendakwa beliau hanya dimaklumkan bahawa anak lelakinya yang berusia 12 tahun tidak perlu menandatangani apa-apa dokumen dan boleh pulang ke rumah selepas mereka memasuki ibu pejabat SPRM.
Katanya, beliau sudah memaklumkan kepada pegawai SPRM bahawa anaknya masih di bawah umur dan tidak memiliki sebarang harta atas namanya.

“Jika dia tidak perlu hadir, mengapa perkara ini tidak dijelaskan sebelum seorang kanak-kanak 12 tahun dibawa ke ibu pejabat agensi antirasuah? Inilah perkara mengarut yang menjadi intipati insiden ini,” katanya.

Semalam, Saravanan mengkritik justifikasi SPRM berhubung keperluan anak lelakinya yang berusia 12 tahun hadir di ibu pejabat agensi itu pada Isnin sebagai 'sama sekali tidak masuk akal', menegaskan bahawa kanak-kanak bawah umur tidak perlu dilibatkan dalam urusan tersebut.
Beliau turut menuduh SPRM gagal menggunakan pertimbangan asas dan kewajaran akal berhubung seorang kanak-kanak berusia 12 tahun, menyifatkannya sebagai amat dikesali.
Tambahnya, dakwaan Halim bahawa 'tiada sesiapa untuk menjaga' anak-anaknya di rumah, justeru perlu 'ikut sekali' adalah tidak relevan serta berniat memperlekeh.

Beliau sebelum ini turut melontarkan kritikan serupa terhadap SPRM sebelum hadir ke ibu pejabat agensi itu bersama keluarganya pada Isnin, menegaskan bahawa notis pengisytiharan harta yang kononnya mahu diserahkan kepada anaknya itu sepatutnya boleh sahaja diserahkan melalui beliau selaku bapa.

21a6489a23d351e3: KUALA LUMPUR: Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and artiste Bella Astillah said the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali was cheerful and in high spirits when they last met her, three days before her death.

c006366c1caa432a: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated Malaysian athletes on winning three more gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games in Japan today, describing the achievement as a proud accomplishment that reflected their outstanding ability and determination.

64ac1de380c805ed: Microsoft plans to roll out Excel Canvas through October, adding Copilot-generated reports to its veteran spreadsheet. Excel Canvas "transforms workbook data into a polished report containing visualizations, metrics, and insights," said Microsoft. The reports automatically refresh as the underlying data changes. Users need access to Copilot in Excel and can tweak reports through natural language prompts. Presumably along the lines of "Why the heck did you use that as the x-axis?" Lately, Microsoft has been relentlessly fiddling with Excel. Last week it added an opt-in feature to allow multiple values in the same cell, potentially complicating life for third-party tools that expect one value per cell. Earlier Copilot additions have met resistance or been withdrawn. Earlier this year, there were howls of outrage from users when a Copilot Dynamic Action Button was unceremoniously dropped onto their workspaces. In response, Microsoft swiftly allowed users to send it to the toolbar. Microsoft also abandoned the COPILOT() function in August this year, barely 12 months after introducing it, saying it had "decided not to move forward with this feature." The function carried a warning that its output should be checked for accuracy, particularly when used for business decisions or reports. Hardly reassuring when the spreadsheet feeds the accounts. Automatically refreshing reports could save users some work, provided Copilot selects appropriate metrics and charts. Canvas also enters a crowded market: businesses already using dashboard tools will need a reason to add another. ®
930f3804fec05ef3: NEW DELHI: Indian protesters rallied in New Delhi and Mumbai on Friday, including members of the popular youth-led "cockroach" party, demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner over alleged voter-roll irregularities.
Police deployed in large numbers as protesters waved the national flag and chanted slogans against the Election Commission of India (ECI), demanding its chief, Gyanesh Kumar, step down.
A newspaper investigation by The Indian Express last month alleged impropriety during a large-scale voter-roll revision that has struck millions of names from lists.
The ECI, India's constitutional body responsible for conducting elections, has rejected allegations of wrongdoing, while Kumar has not commented.
Hundreds of people gathered on roads around Jantar Mantar, a government-designated protest site in the heart of New Delhi, which was sealed off behind police barricades.
"My motivation is our future," 19-year-old protester Nidhi Sharma, a Delhi University student, told AFP. "I have to vote."

Supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party – which began in May as a satirical online movement – meanwhile rallied in Mumbai's Shivaji Park in their first protests since July, when their nationwide campaign helped oust the education minister.
Opposition politicians have accused the ECI of acting at the behest of prime minister Narendra Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
At the Delhi protest, Mina Giri, 38, said her name had been removed from the rolls even though she has lived in the capital for 15 years and voted in previous elections.
"How could my fundamental right be taken away from me?" she said.
'Right to vote'
Another protester, Imran, 18, said his family had been left off the list.
"Because of this, we are struggling to get our other official documents," preventing them from receiving government benefits, he said.
"We are poor, don't have a lot and are dependent on it."
Police detained multiple protesters in Delhi, put them on buses and dropped them off elsewhere, but some returned to the Jantar Mantar site on foot.
"No matter how many times they do this, we are going to return and protest," said Sahana, an advocate who was picked up by police but then walked back 2km (a mile) to rejoin the demonstration.
"You cannot take away our right to walk, can you?" she said.
Mobile internet services were also suspended in the area.

Ten years ago, I watched a program I helped build stun the world by beating Go champion Lee Sedol. a47ca63a74a46042: SEOUL: Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea's leader, called Seoul "despicable" on Friday after it demanded an apology over a demilitarised zone blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers.

Pyongyang has denied being behind a landmine blast that caused severe injuries to three soldiers last month inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ), the heavily mined buffer dividing the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice.
Seoul as well as the US-led United Nations Command said the blast was caused by North Korean mines laid on the South Korean side of the border.
The South Korean military demanded an official apology this week, accusing Pyongyang of "a clear violation of the Armistice Agreement".
In the first public response from Pyongyang, Kim Yo Jong, the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said South Korea "even called for an apology" and added that it is "really despicable".

Her statement may dampen hopes of smoother relations between the neighbours after South Korea's dovish President Lee Jae Myung had urged Pyongyang to return to dialogue, even as his military called for an apology.
Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war as the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce, not a peace treaty.

Since 2024, after Kim Jong Un designated South Korea as his country's "principal enemy", Pyongyang's military has laid mines and built anti-tank barriers along the frontier as part of efforts to permanently seal it off.
The mines responsible for last month's blast were believed to have been laid as part of Pyongyang's border fortification work, according to South Korea's defence minister Kang Shin-chul.

The UN Command, which oversees the Korean War armistice and the southern side of the DMZ, said Wednesday it had found an active North Korean anti-personnel mine on the South Korean side of the border.
South Korea's Lee, who took office in June 2025, has reversed the stance of his hawkish predecessor, Yoon Suk Yeol, offering nuclear-armed Pyongyang talks without preconditions.

On Thursday, a day after the South Korean military demanded an apology, Lee said that he hoped the North would "join us now on the path of restoring trust and resuming dialogue, following a long interruption".
"My administration will consistently pursue practical measures to reduce military tensions between the two Koreas," he said.
'Mocked'
However, Kim Yo Jong ridiculed Lee's latest overture, calling it "the climax of the farce that everyone should watch".

South Korea's opposition People Power Party responded by accusing Lee of failing to criticise Pyongyang when warranted even as he takes a hard line on Ukraine for disclosing the confidential transfer of North Korean prisoners of war.
"South Korean soldiers have been injured, and far from receiving an apology, we have been mocked by North Korea," the opposition party said in a statement.
"We fail to see how selectively turning a blind eye to North Korea serves South Korea's dignity or the safety of its people."
As a possible response to the DMZ blast, analysts have floated resuming blaring K-pop music across the border, which the isolated North has long bristled at.
But others say Seoul has few realistic options for retaliation without further burdening border residents already exposed to disruption and danger.

The flare-up comes at a sensitive time. US President Donald Trump's recent overtures to Pyongyang raised concerns that Seoul – an ally of Washington – could be sidelined in potential nuclear talks involving the North, which is backed by Russia as well as China.
Lee said last month that Washington should seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of North Korea's nuclear programme and offer sanctions relief in return.

"For the time being, North Korea has good income from military supplies to Russia and uses it to balance China, hence little interest in normalisation with Japan, South Korea or even the US," Vladimir Tikhonov, Korean Studies professor at the University of Oslo, told AFP.
"However, the war (in Ukraine) will end at some point, the profits from arms exports to Russia will drop, and North Korean diplomatic tone may change, too."
