The abrasive conditions on the low-grip circuit in sweltering conditions — with a track temperature of more than 60°C — have led to forecasts of a three-stop race on Sunday.
McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who was sixth, said he had been impressed by Red Bull’s opening day pace.
“It looks pretty close amongst the top four teams,” he said.
“I think Red Bull have looked very strong through the day. Mercedes as well have looked strong, at points, and obviously Ferrari were pretty good.
“Everyone’s kind of had their turn being reasonably competitive. I think we’re maybe a tiny step behind, but we made a lot of progress from FP1.
“Hopefully, we can keep that trend going — and we’ll see where we end up.”

On a relatively inconclusive day, with teams diverging on planned run programmes, Mercedes’ George Russell and championship leader Kimi Antonelli were seventh and eighth in their heavily updated cars.
“I think at the moment that Verstappen is looking the quickest in a single lap and McLaren are looking quickest on the long runs,” said Russell.
He added that it was difficult to judge the success of Mercedes upgrades to the floor, sidepods and rear suspension.
“When you bring an upgrade to any circuit, it’s difficult to know what your pure performance is and what it isn’t,” he said.

f03decc0cfc5e2aa: Police suspect a 16-year-old was the main operator of KillSec, a ransomware group linked to around 1,000 suspected attacks worldwide. Authorities announced on Thursday that an international operation had seized the group's infrastructure and made three provisional arrests. The German-led Operation KillSwitch replaced the crew's leak site with a police seizure notice. The available information is incredibly fragmented. Europol said the 16-year-old was "the group's suspected main operator," but did not explicitly say this person was arrested. Spanish police announced the arrest of a "minor," a Romanian national residing in Spain, but did not publicly link this arrest to the 16-year-old mentioned by Europol. The US Department of Justice (DoJ) said UK police had arrested Dutch national Fouad Eltibrizi, whom it has charged over alleged cybercrimes in the US and Puerto Rico. It is seeking his extradition. Eltibrizi is the only suspect officials have publicly named. Europol told The Register he was allegedly one of KillSec's negotiators. Authorities have not named the suspected 16-year-old operator. Romanian police (Poliția Română) said a 24-year-old helped establish KillSec in October 2023, although other authorities date the group's formation to 2024. Their statement did not specify whether that person was arrested. Officials separately confirmed to The Register that a Romanian national in his twenties was arrested in Romania on suspicion of acting as a KillSec affiliate. Europol also identified a suspected developer who turned 18 in August and was a minor when some of the alleged offenses were committed. Spanish police referenced a woman who remains under investigation in connection to the case, but was not arrested. The coordinated raids took place on September 30, following investigations that began in early 2025. Ten police agencies from Europe and the US took part, with officers raiding eight properties across Greece, Romania, Spain, and the UK. Spanish police said officers raided a home and an office in an Alicante hotel, while Poliția Română searched four homes. Neither Greece nor the UK has released information about their involvement in the operation. Authorities secured at least 110 TB of data on KillSec's leak site against further unauthorized access. Investigators are examining seized devices and data to identify victims, attacks, and suspects, and trace the group's criminal proceeds. Over the course of the investigation, police took control of five central servers used to manage the group's activities and store victims' data. Security shops Bitdefender and Group-IB also supported the investigation. KillSec uses double extortion, encrypting victims' systems and threatening to publish stolen data unless they pay. Group-IB recently included KillSec, also referred to as "Kill Security" and "k1llsec," in its 2025 top 10 rankings for ransomware groups operating in APAC, LATAM, and the Middle East. The company's researchers said KillSec most commonly preyed on financial services and healthcare organizations, but was known to attack government entities and large enterprises. Group-IB said KillSec also offered stolen data for sale at prices ranging from $5,000 to $500,000. "Servers can be replaced in weeks; the people who build the platform and approve every attack cannot," said Group-IB CEO Dmitry Volkov. "Identifying them and supporting law enforcement in bringing them to justice is what turns a takedown from a pause into an end." KillSec initially offered a Windows encryptor before adding a version capable of encrypting VMware ESXi hosts, deleting data, shutting down VMs, and removing recovery points. ®

ffc887e295d472c8: KUALA LUMPUR: Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman says that he and his bride-to-be, Bella Astillah, cannot be compared to Malaysia's famous power couple, former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his late wife Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali.

Responding to online comments linking his romance to the long-standing relationship of the elder couple, Syed Saddiq stressed that any comparison falls far short, given their incredible legacy and seven decades together.
"I feel we are not worthy of being compared to Dr Siti Hasmah and Dr Mahathir. Not even close, not even one per cent, because their contributions to the country are truly extraordinary," he said.
He pointed out Dr Siti Hasmah's work as a pioneer, especially her medical service in rural areas and her role in inspiring women.

"Dr Siti Hasmah was one of the first female doctors to inspire women. She was the only female doctor in her class in Singapore at the time and won a scholarship. When she returned to work, she was first based in the city. But when asked to work in rural areas, she did not complain," Syed Saddiq recalled. "She went to help families and children learn about modern healthcare and education. She was a true pioneer."
Speaking about Dr Mahathir, the young politician noted that his service to Malaysia is impossible to measure.
"Dr Mahathir is on another level. I don't think I need to list his achievements one by one, because we are still benefiting from them today," he said.
"So honestly, to those who made these comparisons, I know it comes from a good place. But we are simply not worthy to be compared to them, as they are far ahead of us."
Beyond public service, Syed Saddiq admitted that his own romance is only just starting compared to the couple's lifelong devotion.
"Some people might say, 'Maybe not in terms of work for the country, but in terms of love.' Even then, I feel we aren't worthy," he said.
"We are only about to get married and make our relationship official. They shared love and wisdom for 70 years."
He added: "If love is like a book, we are just about to write page one. They haven't just written a single page—they have built an entire library of love stories."
Expressing deep personal respect for the elder couple, Syed Saddiq mentioned that he and Bella look to their journey as a guide.

"This is very personal to us because we are very close to them. They have walked so much further in life than we have. All we can do is learn from them. If we can copy even one per cent of their goodness and service, that would be a true blessing," he said.
He also called on the public to keep the family in their prayers following the recent passing of Dr Siti Hasmah at the National Heart Institute (IJN) on Sept 28 at the age of 100.

"With what has happened recently, I hope we continuously pray that Dr Siti Hasmah is placed among the righteous in Jannah and pray for Dr Mahathir's full recovery. It is not an easy time for him and his family. I hope that with our collective prayers and encouragement, he will return stronger, God willing," he added.
63962a1e23f59e42: KUALA LUMPUR: Persatuan Perusahaan Kecil dan Sederhana (PKS) Malaysia menggesa kerajaan beralih kepada bantuan berasaskan hasil bagi sektor itu dalam Belanjawan 2027, bukan sekadar mengumumkan peruntukan geran berskala besar.
Presiden persatuan itu, Chin Chee Seong berkata, sokongan persekutuan perlu menghasilkan peningkatan yang boleh diukur bagi perniagaan.

"Kebimbangan kami bukan lagi sekadar sama ada bantuan itu wujud atau tidak. Persoalan sebenar adalah sama ada bantuan berkenaan sampai kepada PKS, dan sama ada ia menghasilkan peningkatan ketara terhadap produktiviti, pelaburan, pertumbuhan, serta daya saing," kata Chin pada sidang media hari ini.

Beliau berkata, Belanjawan 2027 wajar menyediakan sokongan kewangan bersasar mengikut tahap pertumbuhan syarikat, merangkumi aspek seperti aliran tunai harian, penaiktarafan kilang, kecerdasan buatan (AI), amalan hijau, serta peluasan ke pasaran luar negara.

Kejayaan inisiatif bantuan itu akhirnya perlu dinilai berdasarkan hasil operasi yang konkrit, seperti kejayaan sesebuah perniagaan mengautomasikan operasi, meningkatkan produktiviti, mengeksport barangan, atau menembusi pasaran serantau, katanya.

Bagi memperkukuh pelaburan langsung domestik, Chin menyarankan Putrajaya menyediakan insentif bagi perniagaan tempatan untuk melabur semula dan berkembang, selain menggalakkan syarikat berkaitan kerajaan (GLC), syarikat pelaburan berkaitan kerajaan (GLIC), serta pelabur institusi membuat pelaburan bersama PKS tempatan yang berpotensi.

Persatuan itu turut memberi amaran bahawa perniagaan tempatan kini berdepan kos operasi yang semakin meningkat, termasuk kenaikan perbelanjaan buruh, bil utiliti lebih tinggi, caj pembiayaan, peluasan skop cukai jualan dan perkhidmatan (SST), keperluan e-Invois, yuran pelesenan, serta kos pematuhan.

Bagi mengelakkan tekanan berterusan terhadap kelangsungan perniagaan, Chin mencadangkan agar kerajaan menjalankan penilaian impak kawal selia dan kos kumulatif secara menyeluruh terhadap PKS sebelum memperkenalkan sebarang dasar utama yang menambah perbelanjaan operasi.

Gesaan tersebut susulan tinjauan terbaru persatuan itu yang mendapati sebanyak 61.6% responden PKS menganggap keadaan perniagaan semasa lebih buruk berbanding 12 bulan lalu, manakala hampir separuh menolak kenaikan lanjut gaji minimum sehingga produktiviti bertambah baik.
0b234480b10439be: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — After exploring Malaysian stories in La Luna (2023) and Badak (2025), Singaporean filmmaker M. Raihan Halim is back with Goreng!, a new action comedy that turns a humble pisang goreng (banana fritters) stall into unlikely cover for a bank heist.
The film follows Johari Hamzah, who devises an ambitious plan to rob a bank by renting a shop directly opposite it and digging a tunnel into its vault.
To avoid attracting suspicion, Johari and his friends run a pisang goreng stall by day while working on their underground tunnel at night.
But their carefully planned heist begins to unravel when their humble shop, Goreng, unexpectedly goes viral, leaving the gang scrambling to cope with a sudden rush of customers.
Things get even more complicated when a food influencer discovers the secret tunnel beneath the shop.
The film stars Sky Iskandar, Nadhir Nasar, Chech Harith, Tony Eusoff and Amelia Henderson, with additional cast members expected to be announced as production progresses.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
M. Raihan Halim, director of ‘La Luna’ and ‘Badak’, returns with the action-comedy heist film ‘Goreng!’. — Picture courtesy of GSC Cinemas
Speaking to Malay Mail yesterday during a media visit to the film’s set, Halim said Goreng! was partly inspired by the entrepreneurial spirit he observed among Kuala Lumpur’s younger generation.
“When I come to Kuala Lumpur, one thing I really love about people here is the hustle.”
He recalled taking a Grab while visiting the city and meeting people who worked multiple jobs, including driving after their regular daytime work to earn extra income.
“To me, I really, really love that hustle of Kuala Lumpur.
“I like seeing the stories of younger people who are hustling to build businesses, whether it is a kopi shop or a burger business.”
Halim said the creative ways young people were building businesses reflected an entrepreneurial streak in the city that eventually became part of the film’s DNA.
While its premise revolves around a bank robbery, he said the story is ultimately grounded in the lives of ordinary people trying to make a living and find their place in a fast-changing city.
The filmmaker also looked to Malaysian comedies of the early 2000s for inspiration, particularly the work of veteran actor and filmmaker Afdlin Shauki, including Buli Balik and Baik Punya Cilok.
“Those are the films that I really love, and I want to bring that feeling back in a modern setting,” he said.
And although pisang goreng plays a central role in the movie, Halim said culinary skills were hardly a prerequisite when he assembled his cast.
“I wanted them as actors first, so whether they could fry pisang goreng or not was fine,” he said.
Halim said Nadhir and Sky caught his attention after he saw them in the drama series Project: High Council and its film prequel Kahar: Kapla High Council.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The four leads of upcoming Malaysian film ‘Goreng!’ film scenes in Kuala Lumpur. — Picture courtesy of GSC Cinemas

Rather than immediately assigning them characters, he said he wanted to spend time getting to know both actors before developing roles that could showcase their strengths while pushing them beyond the kinds of characters audiences might expect.
“I don’t want to make the same kind of film for myself.
“I need to do something different, and I hope when people watch this, they feel that we haven’t seen this kind of film in a long time,” he said.
Filming for Goreng! is currently underway, with production taking place almost entirely in Kuala Lumpur.
Halim said the film is targeting an August 2027 release, although the date remains subject to change.
He acknowledged that finding the right release window is never straightforward, particularly when it comes to predicting which films will connect with audiences.
“To be honest, there is never a good time.
“I think films like Libang Libu are a very good example.
“It just came out of nowhere and found its audience.
“So we’re looking at that.
“I don’t see anything earlier than August 2027,” he said.
The film’s poster and trailer are expected to be unveiled at a later stage.
Goreng! is produced by Clover Films, Papahan Films, Act 2 Pictures, Golden Screen Cinemas (GSC), One Tree Holdings and ACO Media Produksi, with GSC Movies serving as distributor.
b1e0d5be6570d457: SEPANG, Oct 2 — Charles Leclerc topped the times for Ferrari ahead of Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar to hand a timely boost to team boss Fred Vasseur in Friday’s second free practice of this weekend’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The 28-year-old Monegasque driver, who had spoken out in support of Vasseur on Thursday, clocked a best lap of one minute and 37.528 seconds to outpace Hadjar by 0.099 seconds in an uneventful session run in sweltering conditions.

World champion Lando Norris of McLaren recovered from a disappointing 12th place in the opening run to take third ahead of four-time champion Max Verstappen in the second Red Bull, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton in the second Ferrari, and Oscar Piastri in the second McLaren.

The two heavily upgraded Mercedes of George Russell — who won in Baku last Sunday — and championship leader Kimi Antonelli were seventh and eighth, ahead of Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson and Pierre Gasly of Alpine.
Vasseur has been at the centre of speculation since former Red Bull boss Christian Horner described Ferrari as a “dream job” in a recent interview.

The session ended under a Virtual Safety Car deployment after Gabriel Bortoleto’s Audi stopped on the track with a transmission failure, the only incident as the drivers intensified their efforts on a dusty, low-grip surface in F1’s first visit to Malaysia since 2017.
Slithering and sliding

It was clear by the frequent slithering and sliding that tyre degradation was a factor and will be in Sunday’s race, when Verstappen will seek to repeat his victory of nine years ago which came just 24 hours after his 20th birthday.

After a busy interval during which team bosses Flavio Briatore and Vasseur were involved in a news conference, the second session began with Esteban Ocon, due to leave Haas at the end of the year, leading out from the pit lane.
It was a rapid departure as the teams sought maximum track action before what seemed to be an impending rainstorm. The track temperature was 60°Celsius.

As he did in the opening run, Verstappen was soon topping the times with 1:37.785 on mediums ahead of Russell and Leclerc, whose Ferrari boss had called for team unity in the face of speculation about his future.
“Honestly, the big issue we have today is the stability and serenity in the team,” said Vasseur.
“It is a focus that we need to have — and not this kind of question all day.”
In reaction to comments by Hamilton on Thursday urging Ferrari to review their structure, Vasseur added: “It would be a huge mistake to start (and) to not be unified...
“We had a good beginning of the season, for sure. It’s not enough. We want to get more; we want to win more. We want to win the championship.”
As if on cue, Leclerc went top on softs ahead of Hadjar and a revived Norris mid-session, while Franco Colapinto — fresh from his crash in Baku — was nearly six seconds adrift in 22nd for Alpine.
His team chief Briatore had told reporters that the storm last Sunday was now history.
“Sure, I was disappointed when it happened, but it’s another race and everyone forgets, you know?” he said.
“We need to keep looking to the future. The past is the past, and nothing can be done.”
Colapinto faces a 15-place grid penalty for the Baku crash and for taking another new engine.
Hadjar will drop five places for taking a new power unit, and Lindblad moves to the back row with a 30-place penalty for having a new engine, turbo and exhaust.
Leclerc’s Ferrari team-mate Hamilton was struggling to match his pace and inadvertently baulked Gabriel Bortoleto’s Audi, causing him to swerve to avoid him.
The incident was noted by the stewards, while Hamilton reported on team radio that he could not see out of his right-side mirror. — AFP

b8106ddbebaaf45e: BANGKOK: As heavier rainfall looms over southern Thailand in the coming days, authorities are stepping up preparations and readying personnel, machinery and emergency resources for immediate deployment.
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, who also heads the national disaster command, said rainfall in the south was expected to increase as the weather system moved into the region.

Anutin instructed the department of disaster prevention and mitigation to coordinate with provincial authorities, regional disaster prevention and mitigation centres and relevant agencies to monitor the situation around the clock.

The department was also ordered to ensure personnel, pumps, boats and other emergency equipment were ready, while drawing up plans to deploy additional resources and disaster-response machinery to the south, he said.

Southern Thailand is a major destination for Malaysian tourists, with more than 3.5 million Malaysian visitors recorded in Thailand in 2024. The region was badly affected by severe flooding in November 2025, which reportedly claimed more than 145 lives and affected about 3.54 million people.
57990059b71843b5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The ringgit ended slightly higher against the US dollar today after trading in a narrow range, as market sentiment remained cautious amid heightened global uncertainties.

2673bcfb242f19de: BANDUNG, Oct 2 — Malaysia will have to do without the services of Mohamad Faisal Abdul Halim for the Fifa Asean Cup 2026 third-place playoff after the winger suffered a tendon and right calf muscle injury.

Interim national head coach Tan Cheng Hoe said Faisal Halim’s injury was expected to require a relatively long recovery period, but the medical team would do everything possible to ensure that he returned to full fitness.

He acknowledged that the absence of the player, who is nicknamed Mickey, would be felt by the team, particularly as he had been one of the key players capable of posing a threat and providing energy in the Harimau Malaya attack.

“I think the team really misses Faisal Halim’s presence. But because he picked up an injury the other day (against Indonesia), I think he will have to miss the upcoming match. We hope Faisal Halim recovers as soon as possible for the matches ahead.

“It may take quite a long time (for the recovery process), but the medical team will do everything possible to help Faisal Halim recover,” Cheng Hoe said at a post-match press conference after Malaysia defeated Singapore 6-0 in their final Group A Division 1 match of the Fifa Asean Cup 2026 here last night.

In the match against Singapore, Faisal, who was not named in the squad, was seen arriving at the stadium on crutches, with his right leg also fitted with a brace, indicating the seriousness of his injury.

The absence of the Selangor FC player is another challenge for Cheng Hoe as he prepares the team for the third-place playoff against the Group B runners-up at Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta next Monday.
Malaysia finished second in Group A with seven points after thrashing Singapore 6-0, but missed out on a place in the final to Indonesia on the basis of goals scored. — Bernama
e624b6fffc2fdc91: KUALA LUMPUR: Berjaya Hills Resort Bhd (BHRB) is seeking leave from the Federal Court to appeal against a decision upholding the Pahang government's revision of its quit rent, with the application set to be heard on Dec 8.

In a statement today, BHRB said it filed the application on Aug 14 after the Court of Appeal on July 16 upheld the Temerloh High Court's dismissal of its challenge against the revised quit rent rates.

The company said the development came as the Pahang state authorities began enforcement action against its properties at Berjaya Hills on Sept 28, including staff quarters, a central laundry and other essential facilities.
BHRB described the enforcement action as "unconscionable and totally unacceptable", saying it was unreasonable and extreme given that its application for leave to appeal remained pending.

"Whilst BHRB respects the decisions of the High Court and the Court of Appeal concerning the state government's revision of quit rent rates, the company is deeply disappointed and saddened by the courts' decision," it said.
The dispute began in 2020 when BHRB said its annual quit rent was increased from about RM2.4 million in 2019 to RM33.7 million, a 13-fold increase.
The company said it subsequently lodged 11 appeals with the Pahang government between April 2020 and December 2022, following which the annual quit rent was reduced to RM25.75 million.
BHRB said it had paid about RM42.65 million in quit rent and penalties between 2020 and 2026 while continuing to seek a further review of the rate.
"BHRB had no choice but to make quit rent payments under protest between 2020 and 2026, and paid approximately RM42.65 million in quit rent and penalties," it said.
The company subsequently filed judicial review proceedings at the Temerloh High Court in April 2023, challenging the revised quit rent rate.
The High Court dismissed the application on May 29, 2024, ruling that it could not intervene in the state government's policy decision on the revision of quit rent rates.
BHRB said the substantial increase in quit rent and subsequent enforcement action were "unreasonable" and "unconscionable", and could affect future local and foreign investment in Pahang.

The company said it remained hopeful of a positive outcome from its legal action and hoped the Pahang government would continue engaging with it towards a "mutually acceptable and amicable resolution".
f27f4230a3ed0637: Raspberry Pi has raised prices for the 2 GB Pi 4 and Pi 5, citing rapidly rising memory costs. Both models now cost $12.50 more, taking the 2 GB Pi 4 to $67.50 and the equivalent Pi 5 to $77.50. Readers with long memories may recall the $35 Pi 4. Its price "temporarily" rose to $45 during the pandemic and has since climbed further. The board maker reported a 90 percent increase in first-half revenue to $256.9 million, while gross profit rose 79 percent to $59.4 million. Gross profit per board increased 53 percent to $12.20, helped by price rises and stocks of memory bought at lower prices in 2025. Raspberry Pi says that inventory advantage has largely been exhausted. Its advice to customers facing higher prices is to consider older models, such as the Pi 3B, 3A+, or 3B+, and check how much RAM their projects actually need. Price rises have become a way of life for Pi customers. In April 2026, much of the Pi 4 and Pi 5 range saw substantial price increases. A 16 GB Pi 5, for example, currently costs $305 at PiShop – a far cry from its $120 launch price in January 2025, when we wondered whether even that was a bit steep for a Pi. The 2 GB Pi 4 and Pi 5 escaped April's increases, but that reprieve has ended. Prices for other products remain unchanged, including the 1 GB Pi 4 and Pi 5 and the 2 GB Compute Module 4 and 5. The latest round of increases comes as enthusiasts and vendors alike ponder ways to upgrade the memory soldered to the boards. Raspberry Pi engineer Phil Elwell took to the firm's support forums earlier this year to state that newer firmware locked the devices to their original RAM capacity. Pi boss Eben Upton said: "The price of memory will eventually subside, and we look forward to reversing our own price increases when it does." Customers may be waiting a while. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra warned earlier this week that RAM shortages would persist into 2028 and possibly beyond. He added: "We do not have line of sight to when supply and demand will return to balance." ®
19ab54b408c4dc4d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Bella Astillah and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman will hold two public wedding receptions in Muar, Johor, and Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, later this month as part of their wedding celebrations.

The couple announced the receptions today at the Walimatulurus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq press conference at the KLGCC Convention Centre, ahead of their solemnisation ceremony on October 10 at Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur.
The receptions, themed “Kenduri Rakyat” and open to members of the public, will take place in Muar on October 25, followed by a celebration in Kota Kinabalu on October 31.
Syed Saddiq said plans for the two public celebrations came together in less than two months, with the couple working around a tight schedule and the challenge of securing suitable venues.
“Our receptions will be themed ‘Kenduri Rakyat’, where members of the public are invited to attend.
“The concept will be like a ‘rewang’, where everyone can come together to celebrate.
“If the Hari Raya celebrations in Muar alone previously attracted up to 10,000 people, we expect even more people to attend our ‘kenduri’.
“So it will be on a first-come, first-served basis. Even if the food runs out, both of us will still be there to spend time with the guests who attend,” he said.
Bella, meanwhile, said the couple plans to prepare 10,000 special souvenirs for guests attending the two “Kenduri Rakyat” receptions.
She also clarified that the Sabah celebration will be held in Kota Kinabalu rather than Sandakan, where she was born.
Bella, whose full name is Dayang Ara Nabellah Awang Astillah, said she was looking forward to celebrating in Sabah and wanted to clear up confusion over the venue.
“I am really happy to be holding the celebration in Sabah because I was born there, in Sandakan.
“Many people misunderstood and thought I would hold the reception in Sandakan, so I want to take this opportunity to clarify that it will be held in Kota Kinabalu.
“I really cannot wait. We also want to prepare souvenirs, depending on what we can afford, so I am really looking forward to it,” she said.
97b43edd3bb0f8b3: PETALING JAYA: MIC deputy president M Saravanan this evening doubled down on his criticisms of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission over the decision to summon his 12-year-old son to its headquarters to be served with an asset declaration notice.

Saravanan, the former human resources minister, said his son accompanied him to the anti-graft agency’s headquarters as he was made to understand, following MACC chief commissioner Abd Halim Aman’s Sept 25 remarks, that the 12-year-old was required to present himself to receive an asset declaration notice.
Last month, Halim said notices would be delivered to Saravanan, his wife and two of their children, while another daughter who was abroad would receive hers in November.
“With one child abroad, it was reasonable to understand that the other was my 12-year-old son,” Saravanan said in a Facebook post today.
However, Halim was reported as saying yesterday that MACC exercised its discretion and “considered what was reasonable” in deciding not to serve an asset declaration notice on Saravanan’s son.
He said the 12-year-old’s presence at the MACC headquarters did not mean he was there to receive a notice related to the investigation.
He was also reported to have said that Saravanan’s children were likely present because there was no one at home to care for them.
Today, Saravanan claimed that he was only told his 12-year-old son did not need to sign anything and could return home only after entering the MACC headquarters.
He said he had already informed MACC officers that his son was a minor and had no property in his name.
“If he did not need to be there, why was this not clarified before a 12-year-old was brought to an anti-corruption headquarters? That is the absurdity at the heart of this episode,” he said.

Yesterday, Saravanan criticised MACC’s justification for the presence of his 12-year-old son at the agency’s headquarters on Monday as “entirely illogical”, saying there was no need to involve a minor in the matter.
He also accused MACC of failing to exercise basic discretion and common sense regarding a 12-year-old child, adding it was deeply regrettable.
He said Halim’s claim that the children ‘had no one left at home’ and therefore "came along as usual", was both irrelevant and dismissive.

He had similarly criticised MACC before going to the headquarters with his family on Monday, saying the asset declaration notice purportedly meant to be served on his son could have been served through him as the parent.
f365c337c2d178e2: MANCHESTER, Oct 2 — Manchester City confirmed on Friday that it had launched a “comprehensive appeal” after an independent commission ruled the club had broken Premier League financial rules.
The Premier League announced on Tuesday that an independent commission had found the Abu Dhabi-backed club guilty on more than 100 charges.

“Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm (1800 GMT) on Thursday 1st October 2026 the club lodged its comprehensive appeal against the opinion of the Premier League commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter,” the club said.

0b7a62585e9c6249: PARIS: World food prices rose in September to their highest in nearly four years as logistics disruptions and weather concerns affected crop markets, the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization said.

Fears about a severe El Nino weather pattern have pushed international sugar prices to an 18-month high, while a war-related collapse in Black Sea trade pushed wheat futures to a three-year peak early last month.

The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in international prices for a basket of food commodities, averaged 136.0 points, up from a revised 134.0 for August and the highest reading since November 2022.

“We are seeing a persistent and increasingly broad-based build-up in global commodity prices, as disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and the Black Sea combine with climate shocks, putting pressure on energy, transport and key food commodities,” FAO chief economist Maximo Torero said.
“If sustained, these pressures will soon pass through to consumer food prices, especially in food and energy import-dependent countries,” he said in a statement.
FAO's sugar price index jumped 6.1% from August in a third consecutive monthly increase, as adverse weather threatened to curb supply in major production zones.
The agency's cereal price benchmark rose 5.1% in the month, with reduced yield prospects for US corn adding to pressure from disruptions to Black Sea grain trade.
Vegetable oil prices edged up 0.9%, driven by palm oil on the back of strong demand and concerns over El Nino-related production risks in Southeast Asia.
FAO's overall meat index eased 1.1%. That reflected lower poultry prices, partly linked to a drop in EU demand as new import rules took effect.

In a separate report, FAO kept its forecast for global cereal production in 2026 almost unchanged at 2.979 billion metric tonnes, 2.1% below the previous year's peak but still the second-largest harvest on record.
FAO cut its forecast for world cereal trade in 2026/27 by 0.7% from last month, citing lower wheat and maize export expectations amid constrained Black Sea shipping.
8721333e9b3a832d: HONG KONG, Oct 2 — The ex-husband and in-laws of a Hong Kong influencer and model crafted an elaborate plan that ended with her murder in 2023, prosecutors told the court Friday in the high-profile case.
Police discovered parts of 28-year-old Abby Choi’s dismembered body at a suburban Hong Kong property in February 2023, in a case that stunned the financial hub.

Choi’s ex-husband Alex Kwong, 31, his father Kwong Kau, 68, and brother Anthony Kwong, 35, have pleaded not guilty to murder charges and have been on trial since Wednesday. They face life in prison if convicted.
Prosecution lawyer Charlotte Draycott said that days before Choi was reported missing, the defendants bought equipment later used to cut up and dispose of Choi’s body including a mincing machine.
The court was played CCTV footage that prosecutors said showed Choi, 28, getting into one of two vans used by the Kwongs in the afternoon on February 21, 2023. Her last online activity was at 2:44pm.
Other footage showed Alex Kwong parking one of the vans at a different location at around 3:20pm the same day near the same property where police recovered her remains on February 24.
The three men were seen wearing face masks and were “not upset. It’s what they expected,” Draycott told the court, saying that they had prepared a “cogitated plan” to kill Choi.
On February 25, Alex Kwong — who had two children with Choi — was arrested while planning to flee Hong Kong, a day after his father and brother were detained.
Prosecutors also showed displayed a hammer to the jury and cited a forensic report saying that the injuries on Choi’s skull, caused by a blunt instrument, matched the shape of the hammer.
Prosecutors told the jury earlier this week that Choi and her ex-husband’s family had financial disputes over a luxury property which she had paid HK$60 million (RM31.2 million).
The trial is expected to last at least until December. — AFP

a69d20e975215f63: KUANTAN, Oct 2 — A total of 65 commercial spaces and 35 facility management packages worth RM12.7 million are being offered to local entrepreneurs and contractors along the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) service line.

ECRL Operation Sdn Bhd (EOSB), the ECRL operation and maintenance company, said in a statement that commercial spaces such as kiosks and pushcarts will be provided at the service station to offer food and beverage products, groceries and travel necessities, local products as well as souvenirs and passenger-related services.

7addfd5f809d0607: MELAKA: Sebuah restoran makanan Arab di Bukit Baru dikesan menyembunyikan minyak masak bersubsidi dalam plastik hitam yang diletakkan bersama-sama longgokan sampah kering di bilik asrama pekerja dalam serbuan Op Tiris 4.0 hari ini.

“Minyak masak itu ditemukan selepas premis diperiksa dalam tempoh kira-kira 30 minit dan laluan tangga ke tingkat tiga premis telah diubah suai bagi mengelak daripada dikesan pihak berkuasa,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

Mohd Hazimin berkata, penyelia restoran, lelaki warga Yaman berusia 50an, ditahan bagi membantu siasatan mengikut Seksyen 21 Akta Kawalan Bekalan 1961 kerana memiliki barang kawalan dengan keadaan yang menimbulkan syak munasabah bagi tujuan melakukan kesalahan.

Katanya, pesalah boleh didenda sehingga tidak melebihi RM1 juta atau penjara hingga tiga tahun atau kedua-duanya bagi individu manakala denda tidak melebihi RM2 juta untuk kesalahan pertama bagi syarikat.
9a7a5afea589e446: Fortinet is warning customers to lock down FortiMail after attackers started exploiting a critical bug that lets them write files to vulnerable systems without logging in. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-104286, carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and affects multiple versions of Fortinet's email security platform. Fortinet describes the vulnerability as a combination of path traversal and improper handling of null characters in FortiMail's web interface. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit it using specially crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests to write arbitrary files to the underlying system. Writing files to certain locations could allow an attacker to execute code or commands on the appliance. Fortinet says the flaw affects FortiMail versions 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, 7.6.0 through 7.6.6, 7.4.0 through 7.4.8, and 7.2.0 through 7.2.9. The vendor's advisory says CVE-2026-104286 "is being exploited in the wild," although it doesn't say when the attacks began, who is behind them, or how many customers may have been compromised. It has, however, published indicators administrators can hunt for on their systems. These include suspicious files and configuration changes, along with IP addresses associated with the attacks. CISA has added CVE-2026-104286 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, directing US federal civilian agencies to carry out forensic triage and apply mitigations by October 4. Fortinet lists fixes for several affected branches as "upcoming," leaving customers on those versions reliant on workarounds until updates arrive. In the meantime, Fortinet recommends disabling Identity Based Encryption if it isn't required. Where that's not possible, customers should prevent the FortiMail management interface from being reachable from the internet and restrict access to trusted private networks. Administrators should also check for signs of compromise: applying a workaround will not remove any files or persistence mechanisms attackers may already have planted. It's not Fortinet's first encounter with attackers making themselves at home on its network appliances this year. In June, credentials linked to around 75,000 FortiGate firewalls turned up in criminal hands, though Fortinet said the data came from previous incidents and brute-force attacks rather than a fresh breach. ®
10296d4df430e234: MELAKA, Oct 2 — A Yemeni man in his 50s has been detained today for investigation into suspected unlawful possession of subsidised cooking oil at an Arab food restaurant in Bukit Baru here.

Melaka Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) director Dr Mohd Hazimin Jamaludin said 230 kilogrammes of packaged cooking oil worth RM575 were found during an Op Tiris 4.0 raid at the premises at about 1.30pm today.

He said the restaurant, which has been operating since 2014, was suspected of misappropriating subsidised cooking oil for commercial purposes following a public complaint and three weeks of intelligence gathering.

The subsidised cooking oil, comprising various brands, was found in several black plastic bags placed among a pile of dry waste, including old carpets, in a corner of the third floor of the premises, which had been converted into a workers’ dormitory.

“The packaged cooking oil was found in several black plastic bags placed among a pile of dry waste such as old carpets in a corner of the third floor of the premises, which had been converted into a workers’ dormitory,” he said in a statement here today.

Mohd Hazimin said the staircase leading to the third floor had been modified to avoid detection by the authorities, and the controlled goods were found during an inspection that lasted about 30 minutes.

He said preliminary investigations found that the packaged cooking oil was delivered together with other dry goods using a courier service, while the orders were allegedly placed by the restaurant’s headquarters in Kuala Lumpur.

Mohd Hazimin said the Yemeni man, who was the restaurant supervisor, was detained to assist investigations under Section 21 of the Control of Supplies Act 1961 for possessing controlled goods under circumstances giving rise to reasonable suspicion of an offence.
He said an individual convicted of the offence could be fined up to RM1 million or imprisoned for up to three years, or both, while a company could be fined up to RM2 million for a first offence.
Meanwhile, he reminded individuals and companies not to manipulate, misappropriate or deal in controlled goods without valid permits and licences. — Bernama
f78c9c0d81114e8c: KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (PetChem) has named Izwan Ismail as its new managing director and CEO effective Jan 1, 2027.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the petrochemical producer said the appointment was approved at a special meeting today.
In a separate filing, PetChem's board of directors took note of Mazuin Ismail's resignation as the managing director and CEO effective the same date following his retirement from the Petronas group.
PetChem said Izwan, 51, brings over 29 years of experience spanning finance, corporate planning, strategy, commercial management, operations, and technology.

“Since October 2024, he has served as vice-president, group technology and commercialisation, where he led Petronas Nasional Bhd’s transformation of its artificial intelligence and digital ecosystem, as well as its research and development ecosystem.
“Currently, he serves as director of Petronas Gas Bhd and various subsidiaries of the Petronas Group,” it said.
Izwan began his career with Arthur Andersen in Sydney in 1997 before joining Petronas in 2000, where he served in corporate finance, group accounts and group treasury at its subsidiary, MISC Bhd.

He holds a Bachelor of Commerce with a double major in Accounting and Information Systems from University of New South Wales, Australia, and a Master of Business Administration from Harvard Business School in the US.

343351942d5ce764: NAGOYA, Oct 2 — Malaysia’s men’s squash team clinched the country’s ninth gold medal at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games after defeating Pakistan 2-0 in the final at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena earlier today.

The victory saw Malaysia reclaim the men’s team gold, having last won it at the 2018 edition in Jakarta-Palembang, Indonesia. At the 2022 edition in Hangzhou, the national squad could only manage bronze.

It was a double gold for the national squash camp today, as the women’s squad also defended their title with a 2-1 win over Hong Kong, bringing squash’s contribution to the national contingent at this edition to four gold medals.
In the final earlier, C. Ameeshenraj delivered Malaysia’s first point, recovering from a first-set loss to defeat Nasir Iqbal 8-11, 11-3, 11-6, 11-4.
The second point came through Ng Eain Yow, who prevailed in a hard-fought match to see off Noor Zaman 11-8, 6-11, 7-11, 11-4, 11-5, sealing victory for the national squad.
Meanwhile, last Sunday, Eain Yow and S. Sivasangari delivered gold medals in the men’s and women’s individual events respectively.
Speaking after the match, Eain Yow described the victory as especially meaningful, given the effort required to overcome his opponent, including a comeback from a 1-2 deficit.

“Overall, I’m happy, I’m really, really happy. I’m also a bit speechless at the moment because I had to really fight hard and dig very deep. My opponent was playing really well. I don’t think I’ve been challenged like that in the last two weeks.
“I really wanted to deliver the fourth gold. I’m so, so happy to win the fourth and also the ninth medal for Malaysia,” he said.
Commenting on the national men’s team’s success in clinching the team gold after last winning it at the 2018 edition, Eain Yow said the achievement also settled some “unfinished business” for him.
“2018 was my debut, and I delivered the winning point back then. So, it was a big, big experience. But the last edition, I think I let my team down a little bit.
“I was the number one player, and I just lost out to the Indian player. “So, I had some unfinished business this time around,” he said. — Bernama
f4f275deb672ea10: SHIZUOKA, Oct 2 — He is 38 and had trained with the team for only three weeks, but that did not stop Datuk Mohd Azizulhasni Awang from producing an extraordinary ride to win the men’s keirin gold at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games at Izu Velodrome today.

The Dungun-born cyclist from Terengganu said the victory was even more meaningful as he had to compete against much younger riders, including 22-year-old Chinese rider Li Zhiwei, in a high-speed final.

He said the victory proved that all the sacrifices and challenges he had endured leading up to the Games had been worthwhile, especially after joining the team’s training camp in Brisbane a week late.
“I only trained with the team for three weeks. But Alhamdulillah, despite all the challenges, everything went smoothly.
“In the sprint, my timing wasn’t too bad. I closed the gap. It’s just that I couldn’t match the strength of the Chinese rider in the semi-finals,” he told reporters after the race.
However, failing to advance to the sprint final yesterday motivated Azizulhasni to bounce back in the keirin, where he had vowed to give his all in pursuit of the gold.
“I said I would first try to make the final, and if I made the final, I would hunt for the gold. Alhamdulillah, today I fulfilled that promise,” he said.
Commenting on the final, the Pocket Rocketman said the race was contested at such a high speed that he described it as almost on par with a World Championships final.
He chose not to rush to catch the leading group, instead gradually building up his pace before increasing his speed on the final lap to ensure that no rider overtook him at the end of the race.
“I gave them a gap and chased them down slowly. My timing was such that I only came in strongly on the final lap to make sure nobody tried to overtake me at the last minute.
“The timing was perfect and I overtook them all the way to the finish line. It was beautiful, but I was really exhausted afterwards,” he said.
According to Azizulhasni, his achievement also earned recognition from much younger rivals, including Japan’s Kaiya Ota, who is 11 years younger than him, and Zhiwei, who is 16 years younger.
“They also said, ‘You are crazy, 38 years old, how can you still be competing at this level (at the Asian Games)?’” he said.
The victory saw Azizulhasni end his Asian Games career with an overall haul of two gold, one silver and two bronze medals. — Bernama
b8d487a8c2fab588: SYDNEY, Oct 2 — The state government of Australia’s New South Wales (NSW) on Friday reported a second government website breach involving an OpenAI agent, reported Xinhua.

2b60d4cbc8a692f3: The Metropolitan Police has stopped using digital forensics software from Oxygen Forensics while it investigates US allegations that the supposedly American outfit was secretly owned by Russians and developing its wares in Moscow. Scotland Yard confirmed it has paused use of the company's tools and launched a "full review," after US prosecutors last week accused Oxygen CEO Lee Reiber and Russian national Oleg Sergeyevich Davydov of concealing the company's ownership and where its software was actually being built. The Met signed a three-year deal with Oxygen in December 2023. Digital forensics teams use its software to extract and analyze data from phones and other devices seized during investigations. "We have paused our use of the tool while we carry out a full review," a Met spokesperson told The Times. "At this time, we believe any impact to ongoing investigations will be extremely limited. The Met does not share any data obtained from investigations with Oxygen Forensics Inc." The force said Oxygen's software runs on a closed IT system that isn't connected to the internet and was used in less than 0.2 percent of the more than 23,000 actions carried out by its digital forensics team over the past year. The pause comes after the US Department of Justice alleged that Oxygen, which is based in Alexandria, Virginia, presented itself to US government customers as an independent American company despite being owned and controlled by five Russian nationals through a Cyprus-based holding company. Prosecutors claim the same five Russians also owned Moscow-based MKO Systems, previously known as Oxygen Software, where developers actually wrote Oxygen's software. MKO, meanwhile, sold the technology in Russia under different product names to customers reportedly including the Federal Security Service, better known as the FSB, as well as the Russian Investigative Committee and Ministry of Internal Affairs. Oxygen's US customers weren't exactly small fry. US defense and homeland security agencies bought its software, including Homeland Security Investigations, the DHS Office of Inspector General, and the Secret Service's National Computer Forensics Institute. The DoJ isn't alleging that Oxygen's software contained malicious code or was used to gain unauthorized access to customer systems or data. Davydov, 52, was arrested at London's Heathrow Airport last month while preparing to fly to Turkey and appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday as the US seeks his extradition. District Judge Anthony Calloway declined to grant bail, according to The Times, citing Davydov's Russian citizenship and residence and the risk that he could flee. A clerk at Westminster Magistrates' Court told The Register that Davydov, was refused bail because it "hadn’t had enough time to gather important information." The fallout isn't limited to Scotland Yard. The National Police Chiefs' Council said other UK forces also use Oxygen products and have been encouraged to carry out their own assessments. "We are aware of the allegations made by US authorities regarding Oxygen Forensics," an NPCC spokesperson said. "These remain allegations at this stage and we note that US authorities have stated they are not alleging the software contained malicious code or that customer data was accessed without authorisation." "Forces that use Oxygen products have also been encouraged to undertake proportionate local assessments and activity to understand and contain any issues that are identified," the spokesperson added. The allegations are causing headaches elsewhere in Europe too. Romanian authorities have begun terminating their use of Oxygen products, while Latvia's State Police has suspended the software pending an assessment. The Register contacted The Met, NPCC and Oxygen Forensics for comment. ®

9b2dd33bb38bebfa: This week, I officially signed up for an unusual competition. One that rewards competitors for getting younger.

I recently turned 40, and I don’t need reminding that both time and my chronological age only tick forward. But this game is focused on competitors’ biological ages—figures that are meant to provide a better way to measure the age-related health of our organs and bodies.

Over a six-month period, around 500 of us will try to reverse our biological age as measured in a bunch of different ways. There’s even a leaderboard! The winners will include the person who shows the greatest difference between their chronological and biological age, as well as the person who manages to reverse their biological age the most.

The competition is the brainchild of the neuroscientist and physician Christin Glorioso, who is also founder and CEO of NeuroAge Therapeutics. The company offers tools to track brain health and aging and is running a trial to find out if biological brain age can predict the onset of Alzheimer’s disease.

Glorioso says she has several goals for the Younger contest. The first, she tells me, is to “explain to the world what aging clocks are.” Regular Checkup readers will be familiar with these tools, but for the uninitiated, they are basically designed to measure biological age.

Many measure chemical signatures that form a layer on top of our DNA and seem to change with age. But others might involve looking at proteins or lipids in blood. Some are designed to measure functional health, while others predict when a person will die. There are more than a hundred clocks out there, and they probably each capture a specific aspect of the biological process of aging.

These clocks are proving very useful for scientists, who use them to study aging and development in humans and many other species. But using them to estimate the biological age of an individual person is more controversial. They’re just not good enough for that yet.

Part of the problem is that we don’t really understand what each clock is capturing. Glorioso hopes that data collected through the Younger contest might help answer that question. She’s hoping to generate “the world’s most comprehensive clock dataset.”

Some longevity clinics try to get around the limits of biological age testing by using multiple clocks. That’s this competition’s approach too. As a standard competitor, I’ll be sending a blood spot sample to TruDiagnostic, a company that measures epigenetic chemical groups on DNA and offers to reveal an overall biological age as well as a person’s pace of aging and the biological ages of each of 11 organ systems, including the heart and brain.

I’ll get a brain age score from NeuroAge once I complete the cognitive tasks on offer. I’ll also submit some physical measures like grip strength. And I’ll upload a series of selfies to an app developed by a team at Harvard that promises to tell me my face age. That’s exactly what it sounds like—an estimate of how old my face looks.

I’m intrigued to see my scores, even though I know I shouldn’t put too much stock in them. The first time I took a test, four years ago, the company I used gave me a biological age that matched my chronological age, which was a little disappointing and, if I’m honest, a bit underwhelming. A year later, the same company told me I had a young heart but a relatively old brain, liver, and hormonal system. My lifestyle hasn’t changed much since then. Will the years have made much difference?

(Ultra competitors—who pay $4,499 rather than the $999 cost of regular entry—are also offered a range of other blood tests and clocks, as well as MRI and DEXA scans. I’ve got complimentary press access to the standard package.)

Glorioso is also hoping to gather information about the effects of some purported longevity approaches. During the competition, some participants will be offered red-light masks, access to a sauna, or other low-risk offerings that partner companies who are sponsoring the event to varying degrees might want to collect data on. “A lot of these companies just can’t afford to run [clinical] trials,” says Glorioso.

She also sees the event as a public health initiative. A couple of years ago, David Sinclair, who studies aging at Harvard Medical School, and his colleagues estimated that if we could slow down aging in the general population and increase life expectancy by one year, it would save the US economy $38 trillion.

The event officially kicks off in January, but around 120 people have already signed up, says Glorioso. Ultimately, she expects 500 participants. Each person’s six-month run starts as soon as they take their baseline measurements, whenever that may be. A handful of people have already started. “I think the majority of people are going to want to sign up after the holidays,” says Glorioso. “They’re not going to want to be trying to win an aging contest over Christmas and Hanukkah.”

Glorioso took her own baseline measurements back in August. Those initial tests suggested that her biological age was around 10 years below her chronological age. That sounded pretty impressive to me until I looked at the leaderboard and saw that competitor @Fred had a biological age 28.8 years below his chronological age.

The leaderboard is pretty sparse at the moment, as only seven people have logged their baseline measurements so far. Six of them have biological ages tracking low, but one 47-year-old has been given a biological age of 68.1. She’s competing publicly, so I can see the breakdown of her scores. The worst is for the speed at which she can stand from sitting in a chair—by that measure, she’s been given a biological age of 100.

Hillary Lin, a longevity-focused physician in New York, has just started logging her baseline measurements for the competition. She tells me she’s taken biological age tests in the past and that they’ve tended to give scores below her chronological age, which is currently 37. Last year, the TruDiagnostic test put her pace of aging at 0.75—suggesting she’s only doing nine months’ worth of aging in a typical year. “That’s supposed to be quite good,” she says.

If it had been up to her, Lin says, she would have incorporated more blood tests into the competition, to build a fuller picture of a person’s health. And she’s worried that a six-month period might not be long enough to see changes in biological measures of aging. Still, she’s excited, and is already making plans to improve her sleep, diet, and exercise.

But she already follows a high-protein, low-carb diet and works out at the gym every day. She also visits a sauna every few days (sauna use has been linked to improved heart health). Glorioso’s efforts are impressive too. She tells me she’s started drinking a smoothie made from a pond plant that has been linked to health improvements, and that she’s cut added sugar and deep-fried foods from her diet. She’s also bought “a bunch of fancy Korean sunscreens” in an attempt to lower her face age.

I haven’t received my kit or logged my baseline measurements yet, and I’ll wait until then to start setting health goals. I don’t fancy my chances against these two competitors. But at the very least, I hope I can stand up faster than a 100-year-old.

bf1b63f5280d3200: Welcome to another installment of On Call, The Register's Friday column that shares your tech support stories. This week we're taking a detour into tech sales, courtesy of a reader we'll Regomize as "Carson," whose employer sent him to China without first securing a visa. The adventure began when a colleague called with a fateful question: "Can you travel to China tomorrow to attend a sales meeting about our short messaging and notification products?" UK-based Carson was available, but doubted his employer could obtain the necessary visa in time. "I was told not to worry; the company would arrange it," he told On Call. So he agreed to go. "I was up bright and early the next morning when I felt a sharp pain," he wrote. "There was a wasp in the leg of my jeans which had stung me three times. That did not bode well." Nor did the prospect of spending the 12-hour flight to Hong Kong in economy. "Normally I would have been in business class for a flight of that length but there were no seats left at such short notice," he wrote. "It was not pleasant with a swollen and throbbing thigh." At the transfer desk in Hong Kong, Carson explained that he still lacked a visa for mainland China, but that his employer was trying to secure one. After making a flurry of calls, airline staff issued him a boarding pass and told him to hurry or he would miss the flight. And then his employer called with instructions not to board until told to do so. Carson became that passenger holding up the flight until his phone rang again and a colleague assured him that someone would meet him in Shanghai. "I was, indeed, met at Shanghai Airport, airside," Carson told On Call. "My colleague informed me that I was to be denied entry to China because I lacked a visa. A couple of large policemen took possession of my passport and escorted me through baggage claim and into a smoke-filled room." The local police told Carson he would have to pay a fine, but that they would not accept a credit card. "I had no Chinese money because it was illegal to import or export it. So I was marched to a bureau de change that exchanged every banknote I had on me – $250 – for Chinese banknotes." Carson's fine was the equivalent of $247. "I was told I would be placed in a hotel overnight, under guard, and deported in the morning," Carson wrote. His employer intervened and arranged a better hotel, sparing Carson a night sharing a room with Chinese police. Carson might reasonably have expected to sleep after that ordeal. Instead, colleagues piled into his hotel room to work on the sales presentation they still hoped to deliver. His police guards stayed to watch as the preparations stretched through the evening and finally ended at 3am. Carson finally caught three hours of shuteye before the police woke him, escorted him to breakfast, and then to the airport. "I had to buy a ticket back to Hong Kong and oddly, only first class was available. The police took me to the first-class lounge then to my comfortable seat. Only when sitting down with my seatbelt fastened did I get my passport back." While Carson was being expelled, his visa finally came through. He was therefore soon aboard another flight to Shanghai, where he arrived at night and met a waiting taxi driver... who delivered the news that the bid team was now 300 km away in another city. Carson got in the cab and arrived at midnight. "The meeting was with a team representing a state organization. It started at 9am and ended at about 10pm," he told On Call. "I gave a 15-minute presentation but most of the meeting was conducted in Mandarin" – a language Carson does not speak. "After helping to tidy the meeting room and grabbing a quick beer with a Hong Kong-based colleague, I went to bed at about midnight before getting up at 6am for my taxi to the airport." Carson eventually made it home and, in his email to On Call, rated the adventure: "Not my best trip." What's the worst business trip technology has inflicted on you? The first step of your journey to an appearance in On Call involves clicking here to email us your story! ®
e009d974688ddbea: On an afternoon in Seoul in March 2016, I watched a program I helped build put a stone on the fifth line of a Go board in what looked like a gift to its human opponent. Move 37 in game two of the five-game match looked so absurd that some commentators thought it was a programming glitch.

It wasn’t. AlphaGo won the game, ultimately triumphing 4-1 over Lee Sedol, one of the greatest professional Go players of all time. “I thought AlphaGo was based on probability calculation and that it was merely a machine,” Lee said afterwards. “But when I saw this move, I changed my mind. Surely, AlphaGo is creative.”

When Deep Blue defeated then reigning world chess champion Garry Kasparov in 1997, it did so by looking six to eight moves ahead per player and evaluating 200 million chess positions per second, using rules hard-coded by humans. Go is a vastly more complex game. A stone’s worth depends on how distant groups and territory unfold over dozens of moves. Computing even a fraction of the possible outcomes would take a supercomputer billions of years. To win, AlphaGo had to sense who was ahead at a glance and even invent moves no human had thought to play.

That is why many accounts of AlphaGo’s match against Lee portray move 37 as a flash of pure machine intuition. But that is a misunderstanding. It was actually AlphaGo’s powers of reasoning that made this creative choice—and these are powers that today’s AI lacks. If we want future AI systems to produce trustworthy results and really novel insights in fields like science and medicine, we need to equip them with genuine reasoning capabilities of this kind.

AlphaGo is made up of two systems. The first, its policy network, was trained to guess what move a strong human would play. This “intuitive” part regarded move 37 as nothing special—a play that had a roughly one in 10,000 chance of being made by an expert human player. What made AlphaGo choose it was the program’s search machinery, which looked beyond immediate plausibility and weighed the future consequences of proposed moves. It explicitly constructed and searched a game tree with thousands of branches, each representing a different possible future.

A well-known theory in the behavioral sciences, popularized by Daniel Kahneman, distinguishes between two modes of human thought: System 1 is fast, gut-level, effortless; system 2, slow, step-by-step, and deliberative. AlphaGo offered a striking machine analogue of that split. Its networks supplied the hunches—this move looks promising, this position looks won—and its search supplied the deliberation, testing those hunches against the moves and countermoves that would follow. As in human cognition, neither half works alone. Intuition alone would never have opted for move 37, and brute-force search would have struggled to sieve through all the many possible moves.

This is strikingly different from the way today’s AI models work. A large language model picks the next token, over and over. That amounts to system 1 in action—fast, associative, and surprisingly good pattern completion across almost every subject people write about.

Not long after ChatGPT debuted, the field realized that language fluency alone falls short of true usefulness. The apparent solution was to make models that deliberate: Instead of answering immediately, they can now generate intermediate steps that decompose a problem, carry forward partial results, and influence subsequent reasoning—a process known as chain of thought.

The gains have proved real, above all in mathematics and coding. But unlike AlphaGo’s search, this does not introduce a genuinely separate reasoning mechanism: The intermediate reasoning is still produced by the same next-token prediction process, iterated for longer before the model commits to an answer.

Three shortcomings prevent what chatbots do from qualifying as reasoning (in a way that a scientist might recognize). First, these models typically maintain no explicit, persistent, and inspectable epistemic state. There is no open ledger that lays out the hypotheses a model is considering, the confidence it has in various explanations, the evidence it’s weighing, and the unresolved questions it’s holding onto—all things that should be systematically revised as new information arrives.

Second, they lack a clean separation between what the system knows and how it manipulates that knowledge. Knowledge and reasoning are inextricably interwoven in the weights of the neural network—there is no independent, explicitly represented set of beliefs. Third, while the chains of thought chatbots produce look like deliberation, research has demonstrated that the bots often concoct them after the fact, reaching an answer by one route but reporting another.

This is a problem because in the high-stakes applications we all care about, such as medicine, engineering, and scientific research, it matters not only what a system concludes but also how it arrives at its conclusion. When mistakes happen—for example, in medical diagnosis and treatment—we need to be able to pinpoint what went wrong: Was the system’s reasoning at fault, did it draw on invalid evidence, or did it make incorrect assumptions?

This is why I recently left my position at Google DeepMind. I believe we need a fresh approach to machine reasoning—one that draws on AlphaGo’s architecture. AlphaGo maintains a record of what it knows about a given position: the game tree. This data structure contains all the variations, the possible futures, that AlphaGo has considered, each move and position being annotated with judgments made by its neural networks. As its reasoning progresses, AlphaGo updates the game tree and eventually synthesizes the information in it to decide which move to make.

Similarly, for general reasoning a system should maintain an epistemic state that represents what the system holds as settled, what it doubts, what it has ruled out, which questions stay open. Reasoning can then be understood as a sequence of moves that change the epistemic state to advance knowledge and reduce uncertainty: deducing consequences, breaking problems into parts, and—crucially—deciding what question to ask, calculation to perform, or experiment to run next.

Of course, open-world reasoning is harder than playing a board game such as Go or chess. In the real world the current state of affairs is only partially known, the set of available actions is large and variable, and the consequences of actions are stochastic or unknown.

But recent advances in LLMs and other neural models now give us the capability to take on such general reasoning problems. For example, LLMs can suggest ways of tackling a problem on the basis of what is known and what resources are available. They can interact with tools via APIs or code and help assess whether a claim is supported by available evidence.

Most important, to keep the system honest, an independent part of the system must evaluate each move by how much it actually resolves uncertainty, updating beliefs only when the change is backed by evidence. Once these rules are enforced, the model can accumulate certified knowledge and improve its reasoning policy by learning from past reasoning experiences. You can think of such a system as the scientific method on steroids, with the purpose of producing knowledge that can withstand scrutiny.

I do not think we reach trustworthy machine intelligence by making system 1 bigger. Scale sharpens intuition, but it does not make intuition more deliberative. Move 37 mattered because a machine held a position, weighed the possible futures, and chose the move its artificial instincts would likely have rejected.

Society needs such creative moves in drug discovery, materials, climate, diagnosis—fields where the board looks nothing like a Go board and nobody hands us the rules. We will get such insights only from systems that reason—systems whose conclusions arise from an auditable sequence of evidence, inference, and belief revision rather than from a convincing story told after the fact.
Thore Graepel is chair of machine learning at University College London. He was a core member of the AlphaGo team at DeepMind and works to ensure that AI benefits human flourishing.

8b987812ef6b4eea: The Pi coding agent reached its 1.0 milestone on Thursday while being treated for whiplash. One of the core new inclusions is support for Model Context Protocol (MCP), which Pi creator Mario Zechner once dismissed as unnecessary. Earendil, the company formed by Armin Ronacher and Colin Daymond Hanna that acquired Pi in April 2026, explained the about-face by noting that things change. Not only has MCP improved, the biz said, but changes the Pi devs implemented in MCP have made integrating other capabilities easier. "For example, the changes we have made to MCP also enable the use of Jev more easily within Pi," the company said, in reference to the widely noted Jev decision model that has already elicited imitations. "Ultimately what Pi needs is quite similar to what MCP needs: a sandbox to play with in the form of an interpreter." Earendil describes Pi as "a hardened, minimal, extensible agent harness that you can make your own." If Pi were a Python web framework, it would be Flask rather than Django. Nonetheless, Pi has gained some features. These include Codemode, a harness-side sandbox that helps agents issue tool calls, with support for MCP, decision models, and image models; extension support for virtual models; deferred tool loading; cache warming for Anthropic models; mid-conversation system messages; a new TUI theme; and full-screen mode by default. Alongside these features, Earendil has built Pi Durable, described as "a new substrate for building long-running agentic applications." It's a distinct component from Pi, the company explained, in order to preserve Pi's minimalist design. The Pi agent connects the underlying model to tools to manage conversation; Pi Durable represents the layer that orchestrates multiple conversations and handles the storage backend, via SQLite and JSONL. "Pi Durable is that harness," the company explains. "It does not replace the Pi coding agent. It is a framework for building any agentic application, coding agents included. It shares not only code with the Pi coding agent, like pi-ai, but also its principles: minimalism and malleability." ®

541a2bb315dbb677: Amazon Web Services has debuted an agent that it says will evaluate your cloudy environment “as an experienced cloud architect would” and recommend useful changes. The cloud colossus named its bot the “AWS Well-Architected Agent,” a nod to the Well-Architected Framework that outlines best practices for using the Amazonian cloud. Amazon’s announcement says the agentic incarnation of the Framework analyzes AWS environments “against Well-Architected best practices across 65+ AWS services” and then delivers “targeted, contextual recommendations for improving your applications’ cost, security, performance, and resilience.” “It generates recommendations aligned to your declared business goals, delivers implementation packages with every finding, and surfaces cross-pillar trade-offs making it simpler to remediate the findings,” we’re told. The agent also delivers “ready-to-implement fixes” and “provides individual resource findings with specific dollar impact (where applicable) and step-by-step remediation, consolidated findings across multiple resources scoped to your application, and broad architectural patterns and designs with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) code changes needed to align with Well-Architected best practices.” AWS offers myriad services — some of them with overlapping features and functions. Customers often find themselves using more services than they intended, or using services that aren’t quite right for their intended use. AWS is generally happy if customers change to more appropriate services, even when that sees them spend less, and offers assistance from its own staff or channel partners to make it happen. This agent may make some of that human assistance less necessary. AWS is far from alone in suggesting agents should take on some of the chores that human IT professionals perform today - an approach that’s come to be known as AIOps. When your correspondent chats to IT pros about AIOps, they express distrust on grounds that they cannot be sure agents make valid suggestions and feel following bad advice offered by a machine would indefensible if things go pear-shaped. Vendors I’ve spoken to believe IT pros will first cautiously verify recommendations from AIOps systems, and if they see good results allow agents to take more actions without human oversight - but always with the ability to quickly roll back changes. AWS seems to recognize that users won’t go all-in immediately and therefore offers several manual means to apply recommendations the agent suggests, including the command line interface. For now, the agent is available in the US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), and US West (Oregon) regions, but can handle workloads from any AWS commercial Region. It’s only available for users with an AWS support plan. ®
